Handoff · convo-v3-wireframe.html

Conversation v3, build spec

Everything needed to build the conversation page: tokens, every component with its anatomy, sizes, states, data, behavior, keyboard and copy, the state model and API wiring, and acceptance criteria per phase. The wireframe shows the layout. This spec is the source of truth for values and behavior.

Wireframe: design/convo-v3-wireframe.htmlPlan: design/convo-v3-plan.htmlSchema: chat-ui-schema.mdOct 1, 2026

How to use this spec

Each component block lists where it lives in code, its anatomy and measurements, the tokens it uses, a states table, the data it reads, its behavior and keyboard rules, its copy and its acceptance criteria. Every item carries one tag that says whether it can be built today.

TagMeaningWhat a developer does
existsThe data and behavior exist in the current contract.Build it.
deriveNeeds client-side logic only. No API change.Build it, following the derivation rule given.
backendNeeds a field or endpoint that doesn't exist. Each one has a BE-xx id in the backend table.Build the UI behind a flag, or wait for the backend item.
proposalA value or behavior the product team hasn't confirmed. Each one has a D-xx id in the decisions table.Build the default shown, and don't treat it as final.
About sample content. Names like Qlik Analyst, Atlas, Juno, Priya N., the onboarding plan scenario, model names, request ids and error codes are examples only. Real values come from the data fields named next to them.

Build order and ownership are in A11y, QA, build plan. Every schema component appears in the coverage matrix, either with a spec location or with the reason it's out of scope.

Foundations

This part defines every token the other parts reference: color, type, spacing, layout constants, radii, shadows, z-index, motion, breakpoints and icons. It also sets the CSS file layout and how the legacy app/*.css files are retired. Values that exist in styles/v2/tokens.css or truex-design-spec.html are tagged exists. Tokens that only name a literal already in the CSS are derive. Anything else is proposal with a decision id.

Source of truth today: frontend/styles/v2/tokens.css (copied from the design spec Appendix) and literal values across styles/v2/*.css (schema §8). All new tokens in this part go into tokens.css. Components never use a literal hex, px spacing step, z number or duration once their surface is ported.

1. Color tokens

Theme mechanism

existsP0 lib/use-theme.ts · app/layout.tsx (THEME_BOOT_SCRIPT) · styles/v2/tokens.css

Light is the :root default. Dark applies from the system preference unless the user forced light, or from a forced data-theme="dark". Keep this mechanism unchanged in v3.

Anatomy

Light
:root { color-scheme: light; … }
System dark
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { … } }
Forced dark
:root[data-theme="dark"] { … }, identical values to the media block
Storage
localStorage["truex-theme"] = "" | "light" | "dark". Empty follows the system.
Boot
THEME_BOOT_SCRIPT inlined in <head> before paint. <html suppressHydrationWarning>.
Toggles
Topbar theme button and account menu item.

Data

type ThemePref = "" | "light" | "dark";   // localStorage["truex-theme"]
// write(): sets or removes document.documentElement.dataset.theme
// subscribes to matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)") changes

Behavior

  • Every new token in this part is declared in all three blocks. A token left out of the dark blocks keeps its light value in dark, so only leave one out on purpose (brand ramp, tints).
  • The two dark blocks must stay byte-identical. Add a lint check in CI (proposal, D-NEW: dark block parity check; default: a unit test that parses tokens.css and diffs the two blocks).
  • Fixed-in-both-themes colors stay fixed by design: agent badge (#FFFFFF bg, #1F2A30 text), .strap mixes, celebrate scrim rgb(12 15 17 / 78%) with text #F4F7F8. They become named tokens in Agent tints.

Acceptance

  • No theme flash on reload with truex-theme="dark" and a light OS setting.
  • Clearing the preference follows the OS live, without reload.
  • The two dark blocks in tokens.css contain the same declarations.

Button fill rule (v3 AA fix)

Any button that carries text uses background: var(--accent-fg); color: var(--on-accent). In light that is white on #2A72A3. In dark it is --on-accent (#111213, the value the spec shell already uses) text on the #BCDEE8 fill. Icon-only primary controls (send, dock active) follow the same rule so one component covers both.

Behavior

  • Text under 13px uses --ink-2, never --ink-3. This covers .eyebrow, .convo-time, .msg-foot, .sm, .tab-count, .field-hint.
  • --ink-3 is never text on --accent-soft (4.29:1 calculated). Use --ink-2 there.
  • .btn-solid, plan Approve, request submit and .btn-new-style solid buttons move from --accent to --accent-fg. .btn-ghost default text moves from --ink-3 to --ink-2.
  • Hard-coded literals left in CSS become tokens as their surface ports: .badge-name.is-empty #A3AFB5 → --badge-ink-empty, .badge-foot #E3ECEF / #5F6D73 → --badge-foot-bg / --badge-foot-ink, legacy .sheet::backdrop → --scrim.

Acceptance

  • grep -E '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}' styles/v2/*.css matches only tokens.css.
  • Every button with a text label renders white on #2A72A3 in light and #111213 on #BCDEE8 in dark.
  • No element under 13px computes color to --ink-3.
  • --ok, --bad, --warn render the same as the app tokens in both themes.

Behavior

  • Numeric readouts use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums: .msg-note, .msg-foot, .hcard-time, .goal-strip-meta, .in-kpi dd, .in-row-val, .helper-chip, and every new timer, count or cost.

No z-index tokens exist. Eight named layers replace the raw numbers in §8.8. Values stay the same, so the stacking does not change.

TokenValueWhat goes on itToday

Behavior

  • Native <dialog> sheets (.sheet) use the browser top layer and ignore z-index. Keep them there.
  • The docked request card sits in --z-composer, so popovers and menus always open above it.
  • Toasts render on --z-scrim, after the scrim in DOM order, so they show above drawers and scrim dialogs (proposal, D-NEW: toast layer; default as stated).
  • A drawer's own scrim uses calc(var(--z-drawer) - 1).

Acceptance

  • grep -E 'z-index:\s*[0-9]' styles/v2/*.css returns nothing.
  • A popover opened while a request card is docked renders above the card.

5. Motion

Duration and easing tokens

deriveP0 styles/v2/tokens.css

No duration or easing tokens exist today. Five durations and three easings cover every transition in §8.9. The "spec-only motion" rule still applies: no animation beyond the ones listed here.

TokenValueUse

Reduced motion

v3 turns animations and transitions off, instead of shortening them to 0ms as the global rule in tokens.css does today. Infinite animations with 0ms duration stop in an arbitrary frame, which can leave ag-pulse at half opacity.

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  :root { --dur-1: 0s; --dur-2: 0s; --dur-3: 0s; --dur-4: 0s; --dur-5: 0s; }
  *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
  .pulse { box-shadow: none; }           /* solid dot, label carries meaning */
  .spinner { border-right-color: transparent; }  /* static ring with a gap */
  .shimmer { background: var(--surface-3); }
}

Acceptance

  • With reduced motion on, no element has a running animation (document.getAnimations().length === 0 after load).
  • Every animated busy state has a visible text label that still shows with motion off.
  • No transition uses a literal duration in styles/v2 except the agent-dialog decorative set.

existsproposal (≤1100, ≤400) D-NEWP1 styles/v2/shell.css · chat.css · session.css · agent-dialog.css · app/panels.css · app/responsive.css

All queries are max-width (desktop-first). Rules cascade, so at ≤720 the ≤900 rules also apply. CSS custom properties can't be used in media queries, so the values are listed here and repeated as literals, with a comment naming the breakpoint (/* bp-md */). Width fitting beyond CSS stays in JS (fitPanel).

Behavior

  • Panel widths: sidebar --sidebar-w open, 0 closed; activity var(--pw, var(--panel-w)), resizable 360 to 560. The dock (56px) has no breakpoint of its own and stays centered in .bottom.
  • The docked request card pins to visualViewport.height, capped at 50% with its own scroll, so it fits with the phone keyboard open.
  • The page must work at 360px wide with no horizontal scroll. Tables and code scroll inside their own wrapper.

Acceptance

  • At 1100, 900, 720, 640, 520, 400 and 360px wide, no horizontal page scroll.
  • At ≤720 only one drawer is open at a time.
  • At ≤900 Esc closes the overlay panel and focus returns to its dock button.

7. Icon system

Icon

existsderive (9 new)P0 components/v2/icon.tsx · replaces lucide-react in 11 files and 8 ad-hoc inline SVGs

One <Icon name size stroke /> component renders inline SVG from a PATHS map. v3 adds nine icons and removes lucide-react, so every icon in the app shares one grid and one stroke.

Anatomy and sizes

viewBox
0 0 24 24, 24×24 grid, 2px live-area margin
Paint
fill="none", stroke="currentColor", stroke-linecap="round", stroke-linejoin="round"
Defaults
size = 18, stroke = 1.75
Path rule
One d string per icon. Several shapes join as subpaths (M…zM…). Circles, rects and ellipses are converted to arcs, so the component renders a single <path>.
Common sizes
11 (step check, stroke 2.5), 13, 14, 15, 16 (sidebar nav), 18 (dock, default), 20 (empty-state tile). Send is arrowUp 17 at stroke 2.25; stop is 12 at stroke 3. These overrides exist today and stay.

Tokens

Color comes from the parent's color only. Idle icons use --ink-3 (13px and up rule applies to icons 16px and up), active icons --ink or --accent-fg, status icons the matching --*-text token.

Data

type IconName =
  | "sidebar" | "activity" | "user" | "bot" | "plus" | "search" | "home" | "folder"
  | "book" | "gear" | "arrowUp" | "paperclip" | "globe" | "at" | "mic" | "check"
  | "chart" | "table" | "doc" | "sun" | "moon" | "share" | "chevron" | "chevronR"
  | "chevronL" | "upDown" | "x" | "pulse" | "expand" | "shrink" | "spark" | "stop"
  | "target" | "plug" | "pause" | "play" | "pencil" | "lock" | "grid" | "logout"
  // v3 additions
  | "shield" | "shieldAlert" | "shieldCheck" | "code" | "clock"
  | "coins" | "alert" | "retry" | "copy";

interface IconProps {
  name: IconName;      // typed union, so a typo fails the build
  size?: number;       // default 18
  stroke?: number;     // default 1.75
  label?: string;      // v3: when set, role="img" + aria-label; otherwise aria-hidden
}

Lucide removal plan

  1. Add the nine icons and the IconName union in one PR.
  2. Replace lucide imports file by file, each with the surface's port PR or on its own: project-sidebar, connected-tools, sheet, assistant-tools, runtime-item, goal-bar, ui/select, observability/receipt, trace-card, privacy-card, privacy-note. Map each lucide glyph to the nearest IconName. If none fits, add a path on the same grid rather than keeping lucide.
  3. Replace the 8 ad-hoc inline <svg> icons (for example document-icon.tsx) with Icon. Chart SVGs are not icons and stay.
  4. When grep -r "lucide-react" frontend/ returns nothing, remove lucide-react (^0.468.0) from package.json and the lockfile.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Default aria-hidden="true". The control that holds the icon gets the accessible name (aria-label on icon-only buttons).
  • A standalone meaningful icon (a status icon with no text next to it) passes label, which renders role="img" and aria-label.

Acceptance

  • lucide-react is absent from package.json and all imports.
  • Every icon in the app renders at stroke 1.75 unless listed in the size overrides above.
  • Passing an unknown name fails type-checking.
  • No icon-only button lacks an accessible name (axe button-name rule passes).

8. CSS architecture

Stylesheet pipeline and file layout

app/layout.tsx imports only app/globals.css. Today it imports Tailwind, then the five legacy files, then the v2 files last so they win on shared class names, then two inline rules (button { cursor: pointer }, ::selection { background: var(--accent-soft-2) }). v3 keeps the order and shrinks the legacy block one surface per PR.

The new files are the proposal for where legacy-only surfaces land (D-NEW: v2 file split; default as listed). Each is imported in globals.css after agent-dialog.css.

Naming rules

  • One short component prefix per block, matching today's v2 style: .hcard-*, .ag-*, .in-*, .tc-*, .nad-*, .pl-*. New v3 blocks pick a prefix that no legacy or v2 class uses.
  • States are .is-* (.is-open, .is-active, .is-running). Status variants are .s-* (.s-running, .s-paused, .s-done, .s-ended). Tone is .tone-*.
  • Prefer ARIA state over classes when one exists: [aria-pressed], [aria-expanded], [aria-invalid="true"], [aria-selected].
  • No ids in selectors, no element-only selectors outside base.css, no !important except the reduced-motion rule.
  • Values: tokens only. Literal hex, z-index numbers and durations are allowed only in tokens.css and the agent-dialog decorative set.
  • No new class may reuse a legacy name. The duplicated names v2 currently overrides (.composer, .chat-messages, .goal-*, .menu, .menu-item, .menu-sep, .request-card, .request-option, .runtime-item, .budget-field, .sidebar, .sr-only/.visually-hidden, .eyebrow, .muted, .brand, .topbar) keep their v2 rule; the legacy rule is deleted in the port PR.

Each port PR must: move the rules and switch them to tokens; delete the moved rules from the legacy file; remove the legacy import from globals.css when the file is empty; include light and dark screenshots at 1280, 720 and 400px; and pass the grep checks in this part. Step 6 can land any time.

Tailwind decision proposal D-NEW

Tailwind v4 is loaded through @tailwindcss/postcss with no config, and no component uses a utility class, so it only contributes Preflight. components.json is a shadcn config, with only ui/button.tsx and ui/select.tsx, both mapped to legacy classes through cva. Default: drop Tailwind. Replace Preflight with a short reset at the top of base.css (*{box-sizing:border-box}, margin resets, button{font:inherit;color:inherit}, img{display:block;max-width:100%}), then remove tailwindcss, @tailwindcss/postcss and the PostCSS plugin. Remove components.json, ui/button and ui/select once their callers use v2 primitives. This is the last step of the track, after step 4.

10. Copy-paste token source

The full v3 styles/v2/tokens.css token blocks. The two dark blocks are identical. Values marked proposal in this part are included with their default, and a comment names the decision.

/* styles/v2/tokens.css (v3). Single source of truth. No literal values in components. */
:root {
  /* brand ramp (light only) */
  --brand-50: #F8FCFD; --brand-100: #F4FAFC; --brand-200: #EAF5F8; --brand-300: #D8EBF0;
  --brand-400: #BCDEE8; --brand-500: #3691CD; --brand-600: #2A7DB4; --brand-700: #226A9B;

  /* surfaces and lines */
  --bg: #FFFFFF; --surface: #FFFFFF; --surface-2: #FFFFFF; --surface-3: #F6F9FA;
  --line: #E3ECEF; --line-strong: #D8E0E4; --border-control: #D8E0E4;

  /* ink */
  --ink: #1F2A30; --ink-2: #5F6D73;
  --ink-3: #67757C;              /* v3 AA fix, was #849198 */
  --ink-disabled: #B4BEC3;

  /* accent */
  --accent: #3691CD; --accent-2: #2A7DB4; --accent-hover: #2A7DB4; --accent-pressed: #226A9B;
  --accent-soft: #EAF5F8; --accent-soft-2: #BCDEE8; --signature: #BCDEE8;
  --accent-fg: #2A72A3;          /* blue text, focus ring, AND text-button fill (v3) */
  --accent-text: #2A72A3;
  --accent-fg-hover: #226A9B;    /* proposal D-NEW */
  --accent-fg-pressed: #1E5F8C;  /* proposal D-NEW */
  --accent-ink: #1F2A30; --on-accent: #FFFFFF;
  --warn: #7D5D1D;

  /* status */
  --success-bg: #E7F4ED; --success-text: #35624E;
  --warning-bg: #FFF3D9; --warning-text: #7D5D1D;

Shell and navigation

The page frame, the sidebar, the topbar, the dock, ⌘K, the empty hero, account and share, the shared popover, sheet and toast primitives, error pages, the keyboard map and responsive rules. Today's shell (schema §1) already has a grouped chat list, a title-only palette, a greeting hero, a magnifying dock and four global hotkeys. v3 mounts projects in the sidebar, gives every row a live state, drives every status surface from one derived turn state, turns ⌘K into one search for chats, commands, agents and turns, and publishes every shortcut on a help sheet.

Placement rule from the wireframe: content is inline in the stream, status is pinned to the topbar, the goal strip and the session panel, and diagnostics stay folded. The shell owns the status edges. Its contents come from Composer, Requests and Needs you, Agents, helpers, goals and Session panel.
Sample content in this section (Qlik Analyst, Priya Raman, "Onboarding plan for new analysts", "Analyst onboarding", Google Drive) is an example. Names, titles and counts always come from the data fields named next to them.

App-level state owned by Home

Home state and derived values

existsderiveP1 app/page.tsx · Home (default export, "use client") · new lib/turn-state.ts

Home owns all workspace state (schema §1 "App-level state"). v3 keeps every existing field and name, adds a few local fields, and replaces the ad hoc stateText chain with one deriveTurnState() that every status surface reads.

Data

// app/page.tsx. Existing fields keep their names, types and initial values.
interface HomeState {
  // data and session (exists)
  agents: AgentSummary[];               // []
  agentId: string;                      // ""
  sessions: PublicSession[];            // []
  session: Session | null;              // null = draft
  approvalModes: ApprovalModesConfig;   // approvalModesOff
  draftMode: ApprovalMode | null;
  entries: Entry[];
  events: DomainEvent[];                // last 100 of selected types
  pending: PendingRequest[];
  plan: PlanStep[];
  goal: Goal | null;
  goalReview: GoalReview | null;
  failure: TurnFailure | null;
  subAgents: SubAgentState;
  loading: boolean;                     // true until GET /api/agents settles
  busy: boolean;                        // send in flight or turn running
  running: boolean;                     // turn in progress
  status: string;                       // "Not connected" | "Reconnecting" | "Disconnected" | ...
  streamKey: number;
  slowReconnect: boolean;               // after 30s reconnecting
  retrying: boolean;
  sessionsFailed: boolean;
  error: string; errorDetail: ErrorRef | null;
  draftProjectId: string | null;

  // layout (exists)
  panels: { sidebar: boolean; activity: boolean };
  panelSizes: Record<"list" | "detail", PanelSize>;   // { list: "min", detail: "max" }
  helperOpen: boolean;
  vw: number;                           // 1440, then innerWidth
  paletteOpen: boolean;
  pop: null | "agent" | "user" | "share" | "needs";  // "share" BE-19, "needs" derive (new members)
  agentDialogOpen: boolean;
  panel: "mcp" | "tools" | "agents" | null;
  composerFocused: boolean;
  shellReady: boolean;

  // new local state
  stopRequested: boolean;               // derive: set by stopTurn(), cleared on turn.completed or a 409 from interrupt
  lastTurnEnd: "completed" | "interrupted" | null;  // derive: from the last turn.completed event, reset on send
  sessionsLoaded: boolean;              // derive: first GET /api/sessions settled (success or failure)
  helpOpen: boolean;                    // derive: keyboard shortcuts sheet
  sidebarFilter: "active" | "needs" | "archived";   // "needs" and "archived" BE-16
  paletteScope: "all" | "chats" | "commands" | "agents" | "turns";
  me: Me | null;                        // BE-17
  toasts: Toast[];                      // proposal D-NEW-5
}

// Derived on every render. None of these are stored.
interface ShellDerived {
  empty: boolean;              // !session && !entries.length (exists)
  fit: Fit;                    // fitPanel(vw, PANEL_W[size], CHAT_MIN[size], panels.sidebar, panels.activity) (exists)
  sidebarShown: boolean;       // panels.sidebar && fit.sidebar (exists)
  agent: AgentSummary | null;  // agents.find(a => a.id === agentId)
  crumbTitle: string;          // exists, see Topbar
  crumbProject: Project | null;// derive: projects.projects.find(p => p._id === session?.projectId)
  turn: TurnView;              // derive: deriveTurnState(), see Topbar
  needsYou: NeedsYouItem[];    // derive: spec in #requests; the topbar shows .length
  toolHealth: ToolHealth;      // derive now, BE-06 for live server state
  recent: PublicSession[];     // derive: first 3 sessions, excluding session?._id
  noAgents: boolean;           // !loading && agents.length === 0
}

Behavior

  • Every status surface (topbar pill, helper chip, dock badge, Needs-you count, sidebar dot of the open row, live region) reads turn. No surface computes its own state.
  • stopTurn() sets stopRequested = true before it pauses the goal and calls interrupt. It clears on turn.completed, on a 409 from interrupt (the turn already ended), and on session change.
  • lastTurnEnd resets to null when submitInput() starts a turn and when open(id) or startDraft() runs.
  • Only one of pop, paletteOpen, helpOpen and a Sheet (panel) is open at a time. Opening one closes the others.
  • On mount (exists): health check, GET /api/agents, GET /api/sessions, loadApprovalModes(), loadDelegation(), open ?session=. New: GET /api/me (BE-17) and useProjects() mounted in the sidebar.

Acceptance

  • Grepping for stateText finds only deriveTurnState() and its tests.
  • Pill, dock badge, helper chip and Needs-you count never disagree in any state from the turn state table.
  • Opening the palette while a popover is open closes the popover.
Values tagged proposal with D-01 come from the v3 wireframe (design/.cv3-parts/map.html, nav.html) and are the target until high-fidelity screens replace them. Spacing, z-index and motion values below are written as px and ms. Use the matching --sp-*, --z-*, --dur-* and --ease-* tokens from Foundations.

Frame and layout

Shell, Panel and the layout grid

existsP1 components/v2/shell.tsx (Shell, Panel) · lib/fit-panel.ts · styles/v2/shell.css

One flex row: sidebar panel, stage, activity (session) panel. Panels clip-reveal: the outer aside animates width and opacity, the inner card keeps its fixed width so content never reflows mid-animation. fitPanel() decides the panel width, whether the sidebar may show beside it, and whether the panel floats.

fitPanel rules

// lib/fit-panel.ts (exists, unchanged)
export const PANEL_W = { min: 360, max: 560 } as const;
export const CHAT_MIN = { min: 480, max: 640 } as const;
export const SIDEBAR_W = 268;
export const GAP = 10;
export interface Fit { width: number; sidebar: boolean; overlay: boolean }
export function fitPanel(vw, want, chatMin, sidebarOpen, panelOpen): Fit;

width = min(want, vw - 20)
chat  = vw - 20 - width - 10
#Condition (first match wins)sidebar allowedoverlay
1vw ≤ 720!panelOpen (one drawer at a time)false
2!panelOpen || vw ≤ 900truefalse (CSS makes the panel a drawer at ≤900)
3!sidebarOpen || chat - 268 - 10 ≥ chatMintrue!sidebarOpen && chat < chatMin
4chat ≥ chatMinfalse (sidebar yields)false
5otherwisefalsetrue
Panel sizeSidebar and docked panelSidebar hidden, panel dockedPanel floats
min (360 / 480)vw ≥ 1148901 to 1147 (sidebar requested)never above 900
max (560 / 640)vw ≥ 15081230 to 1507901 to 1229
If D-NEW-1 (rail) ships, the rail takes 44px plus a 10px gap whenever the sidebar is closed at vw > 720. fitPanel then needs a RAIL_W = 44 term: chat = vw - 20 - width - 10 - (sidebarOpen ? 0 : RAIL_W + GAP). Without the rail, keep the function unchanged. The known 10px drift (the closed sidebar's gap stays in flow) is fixed by giving the closed sidebar margin-right: -10px.

Tokens

Frame: --bg behind the shell. Cards: --surface, --line, --radius, --shadow-sm; drawers --shadow-lg. Stage --surface-2. Rail active --accent-soft / --accent-fg, rest --ink-2.

States

StateTriggerVisual change
Pre-readyFirst paintNo transitions. At ≤900 both panels forced closed.
Panel closedopen=falseWidth 0, opacity 0, aria-hidden and inert on the aside.
Panel dockedfit.overlay=false, vw > 900In flow beside the stage.
Panel overlayfit.overlay=true or vw ≤ 900Fixed drawer, --shadow-lg, z 30.
Sidebar yieldsfit.sidebar=falseSidebar renders closed even though panels.sidebar is true; rail (D-NEW-1) shows.

Behavior

  • toggleSidebar() (exists): if shown, close. Opening wins: with the panel open and the sidebar not allowed at the current size, the panel drops from max to min if min fits, else the panel closes.
  • toggleActivity() (exists): closing calls follow.dismiss(). Follow activity (lib/auto-tab.ts, useFollowActivity) may switch tabs (300ms batch, 8000ms manual hold, 60s stale) and only opens the panel when vw > 900, the user did not dismiss it this turn, and opening leaves an open sidebar in place. Tab rules are in Session panel.
  • Resize (exists): crossing from >900 to ≤900 closes both panels.
  • Panels start closed on every load (exists). Persisting panels is not in scope for v3.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Sidebar aside aria-label="Conversations", activity aside aria-label="Session activity". Closed panels are inert, so nothing inside takes focus.
  • Opening a panel with a hotkey does not move focus. Opening it with a button moves focus to the panel's first control only when it is an overlay drawer.
  • Rail buttons carry aria-label plus a tooltip with the hotkey, same labels as the dock.

Acceptance

  • At 1440 wide with both panels open at min, the stage is 772px (1440 − 40 − 268 − 360).
  • At 1300 wide with the sidebar open, opening a helper detail (max) hides the sidebar and docks the panel.
  • At 1000 wide, max with the sidebar closed floats the panel.
  • No layout transition runs on first paint.
  • A closed panel has no focusable descendants.

interface SidebarProps<S extends SidebarSession> {
  sessions: S[];
  activeId?: string | null;
  activeTurn?: TurnState;                 // derive: turn.state for the open row
  onOpen: (id: string) => void;
  onNew: () => void;
  onSearch: () => void;
  agentsActive?: boolean;                 // now passed: panel === "agents"
  onAgents?: () => void;                  // now opens the agents sheet, not the popover
  renderRowMenu?: (session: S) => ReactNode;   // SessionMenu
  loadError?: string | null;              // "Couldn’t refresh" when sessionsFailed || projects.refreshFailed
  onRetry?: () => void;                   // refreshSessions() and projects.refreshAll()
  busy?: boolean;
  loaded: boolean;                        // sessionsLoaded
  emptyAgentName?: string;                // agent?.name
  projects: ProjectsState;                // useProjects(refreshSessions)
  onNewInProject: (projectId: string) => void;   // startDraft(projectId) sets draftProjectId
  filter: "active" | "needs" | "archived";
  onFilter: (f: "active" | "needs" | "archived") => void;

  onAccount: () => void;                  // togglePop("user")
}
// Helpers kept: convoGroup(createdAt, now) → "Today" | "Earlier";
// convoTime(createdAt, now) → "h:mm AM/PM" today, short weekday within 7 days, else "Sep 3", "" if invalid.

Behavior

  • A session with projectId shows under its folder, not in Today or Earlier. Folder children come from projects.byProject[id]; a fresher title in sessions wins (same rule as ProjectSidebar).
  • Folders sort by updatedAt desc, then name (sortProjects). expanded is the source of open folders. assign() into a folder expands it.
  • Folder row menu: New chat in {name} (sets draftProjectId via startDraft(projectId)), Rename (NameInput), Delete (danger, confirm dialog, see Behavior of the Sheet primitive). Delete copy: "Delete project “{name}”? Conversations will stay in Recents."
  • New project: NameInput inline at the top of the group. Validation from checkProjectName (max 80, input maxLength 120): "Enter a project name." / "Use 80 characters or fewer."
  • Row ⋯ menu is SessionMenu (views root, pick, new), unchanged. Disabled while busy.
  • Filter Active is today's list. Needs you shows rows with pendingCount > 0 (BE-16), plus the open session when turn.state === "waiting". Archived calls GET /api/sessions?archived=1 (BE-16). Until BE-16 ships, hide the Needs you and Archived chips and the filter row.
  • Retry clears the error line immediately and shows it again only if the refetch fails.
  • Agents link opens the agents sheet (setPanel("agents")) and becomes active. This fixes the bug where it opened the agent popover and agentsActive was never passed.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Tab order: search, New, nav links, filter chips, Projects "+", folders and their rows, date-group rows, account.
  • Folder toggle is a button with aria-expanded. Filter chips are button[aria-pressed] in a role=group labelled "Filter conversations".
  • Each row button's accessible name: "{title}, {dot aria text}, {time}". Menu trigger: "Options for {title}".
  • SessionMenu keys (exists): ↓ on trigger opens, ↑/↓/Home/End move, Esc closes and refocuses the trigger, Tab closes.

Priority when inputs overlap (first match wins): reconnecting › failed › stopping › waiting › working › starting › interrupted › idle.

// lib/turn-state.ts
export type TurnState =
  | "idle" | "starting" | "working" | "waiting"
  | "stopping" | "interrupted" | "failed" | "reconnecting";

export interface TurnInputs {
  running: boolean; busy: boolean; status: string; slowReconnect: boolean;
  retrying: boolean; pending: PendingRequest[]; goal: Goal | null;
  failure: TurnFailure | null; stopRequested: boolean;
  lastTurnEnd: "completed" | "interrupted" | null;
}
export interface TurnView {
  state: TurnState;
  label: string;           // pill label from the table
  indicator: "dot" | "spinner";
  tone: "idle" | "accent" | "warn" | "bad";
  pulse: boolean;          // false when prefers-reduced-motion
  frozen: boolean;         // reconnecting: counts hold their last value
}

export function deriveTurnState(i: TurnInputs): TurnView {
  if (i.status === "Reconnecting" || i.status === "Disconnected") return reconnecting(i);
  if (i.failure && !i.retrying) return view("failed");
  if (i.running && i.stopRequested) return view("stopping");
  if (i.running && i.pending.length > 0) return view("waiting");
  if (i.running) return working(i);          // goal / retry label
  if (i.busy) return view("starting");
  if (i.lastTurnEnd === "interrupted") return view("interrupted");
  return view("idle");
}
D-07: a helper request (from a sub-agent thread) turns the pill to Waiting on you the same as a main request. Telling them apart waits on PendingRequest.threadId (BE-02). failure clears on the next send (existing behavior); if it does not, the pill would stay Failed after a successful turn, so the reducer that sets running=true must also clear failure.
Qlik Analyst · Ready Qlik Analyst · Starting Qlik Analyst · Working on goal Qlik Analyst · Waiting on you Qlik Analyst · Failed Needs you · 2

Needs-you count

The count is needsYou.length. The item list, its order and the tray are specified in Requests and Needs you. Inputs: open pending[], a goal stopped for input (blocked, usageLimited, budgetLimited, paused after an interrupt), helpers with an errored or notFound SubAgentStatus, the last failure, and tool problems from tool health. Clicking opens the tray (pop = "needs"). While turn.frozen, the count holds its last value.

Behavior

  • Crumb title (exists): session title from the list, then session.title, then "Untitled conversation"; a draft with entries shows "New conversation"; else empty.
  • Clicking the pill toggles the agent popover (exists, D-02). Its title is "Edit {agentName}".
  • Reconnect (exists) sets status "Reconnecting" and bumps streamKey.
  • Truncation order when narrow: project name hides first (below 1100 stage width), then the title ellipsizes, then the agent name ellipsizes. The state label never truncates.
  • Live region: on each change of turn.state, write one of "Working", "Waiting on you", "Stopped", "Failed", "Reconnecting", "Done" (working to idle) into the polite region. Throttle to one message per 1000ms. The streaming body never goes in a live region.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Tab order: crumb (not focusable), pill, Needs you, tool health, Reconnect, theme, Share.
  • Pill aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded with the agent popover, name "{agentName}, {label}. Edit agent".
  • Needs you name "Needs you, {n} items", aria-haspopup="dialog". Tool health name from the tooltip text.
  • Theme: "Switch to light theme" / "Switch to dark theme". Share: "Share conversation".
  • Pulse and spinner have static fallbacks under reduced motion.

Acceptance

  • Every row of the turn state table has a unit test on deriveTurnState(), including the overlaps: reconnecting with pending, failed with running, stopping with pending.
  • Between Send and the first turn.started, the pill says Starting, not Ready.
  • After Stop, the pill says Stopping until turn.completed, then Stopped.
  • While reconnecting, the Needs-you count does not drop to zero.
  • Share opens a popover and no longer does nothing.
  • Needs you is hidden at 0 and shows the exact count otherwise.

Behavior

  • Scope prefixes: a leading / sets Commands, @ sets Agents, # sets Turns. The prefix stays in the input and is not matched.

  • localStorage reads and writes are wrapped in try/catch; failure falls back to the newest sessions.
  • Index resets to 0 on each query change and clamps to the list.

Esc order (fixed)

Modal layers handle their own Esc first and stop propagation: palette, Sheet, AgentDialog, help sheet. Everything else goes through one window handler in lib/escape-stack.ts, which does the first step that applies and stops:

  1. Close the slash or @ menu.
  2. Exit goal mode.
  3. Close the open popover or menu, then the open panel (activity panel, or the sidebar drawer at ≤720).
  4. Stop the running turn, only when running and nothing above applied.
  • Step 4 runs stopTurn() and puts "Stopping" in the pill. It never runs on key repeat (e.repeat), so holding Esc can't stop a turn.
  • D-06: when focus is inside a docked request card, Esc after steps 1 to 3 cancels that request instead of stopping the turn.
  • Inputs that own Esc (NameInput, Share link field) handle it and stop propagation.
// lib/escape-stack.ts
type EscStep = { id: "menu" | "goal" | "overlay" | "request" | "stop"; active: () => boolean; run: () => void };
export function handleEscape(e: KeyboardEvent, steps: EscStep[]): boolean {
  if (e.key !== "Escape" || e.defaultPrevented || e.isComposing) return false;
  const step = steps.find(s => s.active());
  if (!step || (step.id === "stop" && e.repeat)) return false;
  e.preventDefault(); step.run(); return true;
}

useHotkeys changes

export type HotkeyMap = Record<string, (e: KeyboardEvent) => void>;
export function hotkeyCombo(e): string;   // ("mod+" if meta||ctrl) + key.toLowerCase() (exists)
export function useHotkeys(map: HotkeyMap, opts?: { skipFields?: boolean }): void;
// skipFields (new, derive): ignore events whose target is input, textarea, select
// or [contenteditable]. Mod combos keep firing while typing (skipFields false).
Clash rule: hotkeyCombo ignores Shift and Alt and calls preventDefault on match, so any new mod key steals it from the textarea. New mod combos must not clash with text editing (⌘A, ⌘Z, ⌘C/V/X, ⌘←/→, ⌘Backspace) or the browser (⌘L, ⌘T, ⌘W). Prefer unmodified keys outside fields.

Composer

The composer is the form at the bottom of the chat column and inside the hero on an empty chat. Today it holds the textarea, the Goal chip with BudgetField, the alpha approval-mode picker, Send and Stop. v3 moves everything that shapes the next message onto one action bar: files, agent, model and effort, approval mode and Goal. It adds @-mentions, a visible queue for messages typed during a turn, an explicit Steer button and a Stopping state. The slash-command parser, BudgetField and PrivacyNote keep their current logic.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §2. Target design: the composer boards in the v3 wireframe. In this section page means Home in frontend/app/page.tsx. The page's busy means a request is in flight. The page's running means a turn is streaming. Composer receives running through a prop that is also called busy.

Contrast rule for this section: Send, the file icon tile and any other filled button with light text use the --accent-fg fill, not --accent. Text under 13px uses --ink-2. Spacing, z-index and motion tokens (--sp-*, --z-*, --dur-*, --ease-*) come from the Foundations part. The raw values below are today's CSS, so a token replaces each one at the same value.

}
export const PLACEHOLDERS = [
  "Ask anything, or type / for commands",
  "Summarize last week's pipeline changes",
  "Compare Q2 vs Q3 revenue by region",
  "Draft a reply to the customer escalation",
] as const;
export const GOAL_PLACEHOLDER =
  "Describe the outcome you want. The assistant works until it’s done.";

Behavior

  • Placeholder precedence: goal mode → GOAL_PLACEHOLDER (import it; the page inlines the string today); running → "Type to queue. Steer sends into this turn." proposal D-05; empty → rotating; else PLACEHOLDERS[0]. Today's running placeholder "Add a thought to steer the current turn…" is wrong under D-05, because Enter queues.
  • Rotation: useRotatingPlaceholder(active), active = empty && !composerFocused && !text && !goalMode. Every 3200ms, index (i+1) % 4. Index kept when paused. Instant swap, no transition.
  • SmoothTextarea caret: spring {stiffness:500, damping:30, mass:0.5}. SWEEP_LIMIT = 48px: on a line change a wider horizontal move snaps. Caret hides when unfocused, disabled, range selected, scrolled out of view or on window blur. Reduced motion or width change: caret jumps. Recomputes on value or disabled change (microtask), selectionchange, font load, scroll and ResizeObserver.
  • Message length has no max. Only text.trim() non-blank is required.
  • onChange: setText(value), setCommandOpen(!goalMode && value.startsWith("/")), setCommandIndex(0), clear notice, recompute the mention query.
  • Entry points that fill the textarea: startGoal(template), applyPrompt(prompt) ("/goal" → startGoal(), /-prefixed opens the slash menu), ChatMessages.onPrompt/onCommand, askSuggestion. Each sets text, closes menus and focuses with the caret at the end.
  • Reduced motion: .send, .composer { transition: none }.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Textarea: aria-label "Goal" in goal mode, else "Message"; aria-describedby="composer-hint"; combobox attributes while a menu is open (see Slash menu and Mention picker).
  • #composer-hint (.sr-only): "Type / for commands, @ to mention. Enter to send, Shift + Enter for a new line." proposal D-NEW-01. Today: "Type / for commands. Enter to send, Shift + Enter for a new line."
  • Focus ring on the frame shows only for textarea focus. Chips keep their own :focus-visible outline (2px --accent, offset 2px).

Acceptance

  • Typing 12 lines grows the textarea to 240px, then it scrolls inside; the bar does not move off screen.
  • Hero textarea is 76px tall when empty; thread textarea is 60px.
  • Focusing a chip does not show the frame focus ring.
  • The hero placeholder rotates every 3200ms only while empty, unfocused and not in goal mode.
  • With reduced motion on, the caret jumps and the frame has no transition.

Data

// lib/document-kind.ts (exists)
export const uploadAccept =
  ".pdf,.docx,.xlsx,.pptx,.txt,.md,.csv,.tsv,.abap,.cds,.json,.xml,.yaml,.sql,.js,.ts";
// shared/assistant-capabilities.ts (exists)
interface ConversationFile { id: string; name: string; size: number; createdAt: string;
  mediaType: string; sourceId?: string; kind?: "visualization"; title?: string;
  description?: string; mode?: "inline" | "wide"; }
// POST /api/sessions/:id/documents  body { name: string; base64: string } → 201 ConversationFile
// Limits: 1 byte to 1 MB per file, max 50 files / 25 MB per conversation.

// new, client only
interface DraftFile {
  key: string;                     // client uuid
  file: File;
  state: "held" | "uploading" | "uploaded" | "error";
  loaded: number;                  // bytes sent
  result?: ConversationFile;
  error?: string;
}

Behavior

  • Validate size, emptiness, extension and conversation totals on the client first. Invalid files never send a request.
  • With a session: upload starts on pick, up to 2 files at a time proposal D-NEW-04. Use XHR for progress; fetch has no upload progress.
  • Without a session: files are held. On the first Send, ensureSession() runs, held files upload, then the message sends. If any upload fails, the message does not send, the draft stays and the failed chip shows Retry proposal D-NEW-03.
  • Send and Steer are disabled while any chip is uploading. Error chips do not block Send; they are not sent.
  • Remove on an uploaded chip only removes it from the draft. The file stays in the conversation (no delete endpoint). Its row in the Tools panel stays.
  • After a successful send, uploaded chips clear. Today's auto prompt 'Read the uploaded document "{name}" and summarize its key points.' is not inserted from the composer; the person writes their own message.
  • Drag and drop onto the composer and paste of files use the same path. Drop target shows the focus border.
  • Uploaded files feed the Files group of the mention picker.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Attach: aria-label="Attach files", title "Attach files (1 MB each)".
  • The chip list is role="list" aria-label="Attached files"; each chip is a listitem.
  • Error chips use role="alert" once. Progress is not announced per tick; announce "Uploaded {name}" in the composer polite region on finish.
  • Remove button: aria-label="Remove {name}". After removing, focus moves to the next chip's button, else the textarea.

Acceptance

  • A 4.2 MB file shows "Choose a document of up to 1 MB." with no network request.
  • A dropped .py file is rejected with the wrong-type copy.
  • Send is disabled while a chip shows a progress bar.
  • Files picked on a new chat upload only after Send, and the message waits for them.
  • Tools panel keeps listing uploaded files; its upload control is removed.

}

Behavior

Behavior

  • Accepted: 50000, 50,000, 50_000, 50k, 1, 10000k. Rejected: 0, 50m, 1.5k, 10001k, blank custom.

Confirm sends thread/goal/clear, then the new set. Keep current closes the card and keeps the draft.

Data

type MentionKind = "file" | "agent" | "tool";
interface MentionQuery { start: number; end: number; q: string }   // indexes into text
interface DraftMention {                     // client
  kind: MentionKind; id: string; label: string;
  start: number; end: number;                // range of "@label" in text, kept in sync on edit
}
// BE-15: GET /api/sessions/:id/tools
interface SessionToolServer { id: string; name: string; tools: { name: string; description?: string }[] }
// BE-15: send body gains mentions
// transport.send(sessionId, text, clientId, { mentions })
interface MessageMention { kind: MentionKind; id: string; label: string }  // BE-15
// Message.mentions?: MessageMention[]                                      // BE-15

Behavior

  • Trigger: @ at index 0 or after whitespace. An email like priya@example.com never opens it. Closes on space, newline, Esc, blur, or caret leaving the range.
  • Filtering: case-insensitive substring on title and sub; prefix matches rank first, then alphabetical. Max 5 rows per group, fixed group order.
  • Insert: replaces @q with @{label} plus one space, records a DraftMention, closes, keeps focus.
  • Tokens are atomic. The textarea stays plain text; the token look comes from an overlay drawn in the .smooth-mirror layer at the mention ranges. Backspace at a token end deletes the whole token. Typing inside a token drops that mention and leaves the text.
  • Only one menu at a time. The slash menu wins when the text starts with / and has no whitespace.
  • Send: until BE-15 ships, mentions are sent as text only and mentions is omitted. Queued messages keep their mentions.
  • Agent mentions do not switch the agent. They name a helper or agent for the main agent to use.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Textarea combobox attributes while open: aria-controls="chat-mentions", aria-expanded="true", aria-activedescendant="chat-mention-{i}", aria-autocomplete="list".
  • Menu: role="listbox" aria-label="Mention"; group headers role="presentation"; each group is role="group" aria-label="Files|Agents|Tools"; rows role="option" aria-selected.
  • ↑/↓ move across groups with wrap. Enter or Tab inserts. Esc closes. Rows use onMouseDown preventDefault to keep focus.
  • Polite live region: "{n} results" on open, not on every keystroke (debounce 300ms proposal D-NEW-07).
  • Screen readers read tokens as their plain text ("@label"), so no extra markup is needed.

Acceptance

  • Typing an email address never opens the picker.
  • "@ha" lists matching files first, then agents; each group shows at most 5.
  • One Backspace removes a whole inserted token.
  • Without BE-15 the Tools group is absent and sends have no mentions field.

Command copy

  • Blocked while running: "Wait for the current response to finish or press Stop before running a command. Your draft is saved."
  • No session: "Start a conversation with a message before using this command. Your draft is saved."

  • Network failure after send: entry becomes state: "unknown" with "Connection interrupted. Refresh the conversation to check the saved result before trying again."

Commands run as a user entry with command: { method, params, state: "running" } and POST /api/sessions/:id/capabilities { method, params, command: { clientId, text } }. The result replaces the entry (CommandResult, Stream part). On succeeded the draft clears. Commands are never queued: under D-05 a command typed while running is refused with the blocked copy and the draft stays.

Sending, queueing and steering

Submit pipeline

existsP1 app/page.tsx submitInput() · extended with the queue branch

One function decides what Enter or Send does. v3 inserts the queue branch (D-05) and the file wait. Everything else keeps today's order.

Behavior

  1. Silent no-op when: page busy, sending.current, blank text, no session and no agentId, or any file chip is uploading derive.
  2. Slash menu has a highlighted option whose name differs from the text: complete it, stop.
  3. Mention menu open: insert the active row, stop derive.
  4. Goal mode with an invalid budget: notice = budgetHelp, stop.
  5. Parse: goal mode → goalCommand(text, goalBudget); else parseChatInput(text).
  6. Editing a queued item (editingQueueId): only message is allowed. Save the text back in place, restore the stashed draft, stop. Anything else: notice "Queued messages can only be text. Your draft is saved." proposal D-05.
  7. running and kind message: add to the queue (next block), clear the draft, stop proposal D-05. Today this steers.
  8. Goal mode with a goal that is not complete: replace confirm; when confirmed send thread/goal/clear first.
  9. help with a session goes to the server as method "help".
  10. By kind: message → send(text); panel → clear draft, open mcp/tools/agents tab; invalid → notice, draft kept; help without a session → local help notice, draft cleared; command while running → blocked notice; command with no session → only thread/goal/set with an objective may create it, else the no-session notice; command → optimistic command entry and capabilities POST.

send(text): clears the draft, uploads held files, appends an optimistic user entry with delivery: "pending", runs ensureSession() if needed (applies draftMode and draftSettings), then transport.send(sessionId, value, clientId). Success: delivery: "accepted" with turnId and steer. Failure: delivery: "unknown" and the error banner.

Acceptance

  • Double Enter within one frame sends once (sending ref).
  • A retried command reuses its clientId (commandAttempt ref).
  • A stale response from a previous session is ignored (generation ref).

Data

interface QueuedMessage {
  id: string;                  // becomes the clientId when sent, so a retry is idempotent
  text: string;
  mentions?: DraftMention[];   // kept; sent as MessageMention[] once BE-15 exists
  createdAt: number;           // ms, client clock
  state: "waiting" | "sending" | "failed";
  error?: string;
}
type QueuePauseReason = "stopped" | "failed" | "request" | "turnError" | "offline" | "manual";
// sessionStorage key: "truex.queue." + sessionId  (value: QueuedMessage[] with state reset to "waiting")

Ordering rules

  1. First in, first out. Position is the order shown; reorder changes it.
  2. Only message input queues. Commands, panels and help never queue (commands are refused with the blocked copy; panels and help run at once).
  3. Dispatch starts when running goes false after turn.completed and no pause reason is set. Wait one frame so the final assistant entry renders first.
  4. Exactly one item is in flight. The next item waits until the turn started by the previous item completes. Queued messages never steer.
  5. Steer never touches the queue. A steer goes into the live turn ahead of every queued item.
  6. If the person sends a normal message when idle while items exist (for example after a pause), that message joins the end of the queue and Resume starts it. Nothing jumps the queue except Steer proposal D-NEW-09.
  7. An active goal does not change the order. Queued items send at the next turn boundary like any message.
  8. Max 10 items. The 11th Enter shows notice "The queue is full. Send or remove a queued message first. Your draft is saved." proposal D-NEW-08.

Pause reasons and failure

ReasonTriggerHeader copyResume does
stoppedthe person pressed Stop"Paused after Stop. {n} queued."starts dispatch
requesta PendingRequest is docked"Waiting for your answer above."auto-resumes when no requests remain; no button
turnErrorturn ended with a TurnFailure"Paused because the last response failed."starts dispatch
failedsending the head item failed (network or 4xx/5xx)"Paused. 1 message wasn't sent."retries the head with the same clientId
offlinenavigator.onLine false or stream disconnected"Paused while offline."auto-resumes on reconnect
manualthe person pressed Pause in the header menu"Paused."starts dispatch
  • A failed item with delivery: "unknown" is not resent automatically, since the server may have it. Resume first reloads the session and drops the item if a message with its clientId exists.
  • A dead session (410 THREAD_LOST) clears nothing: the queue stays visible, Resume is disabled and each item offers "Copy". Header: "This chat can't take new messages."
  • Switching chats keeps each chat's queue in session storage. Reload restores it in paused: "manual" so nothing sends without a click.

Edit, recall and reorder

  • Edit: stash the current draft, load the item text into the textarea, set editingQueueId, focus. Enter saves in place. Esc cancels and restores the stash. Clearing the text and pressing Enter removes the item.
  • ↑ recall: when the draft is empty, the caret is at index 0, no menu is open and the queue is not empty, ↑ opens the last item for edit.
  • An item being edited is skipped by dispatch until saved; the rest keep their order.
  • Reorder by pointer: drag the grip; drop indicator is a 2px --accent line. Reorder by keyboard: focus an item and press Alt+↑ or Alt+↓.
  • Remove: no confirm. Show a 5s undo toast "Removed queued message. Undo" proposal D-NEW-08.

Keyboard and a11y

  • List role="list" aria-label="Queued messages"; items role="listitem" with tabindex="0" and accessible name "Queued message {i} of {n}: {text}".
  • Buttons: "Edit queued message {i}", "Remove queued message {i}". Grip aria-hidden; keyboard reorder is announced: "Moved to position {i}".
  • Polite live region announces "Queued. {n} waiting." on add and "Sending queued message" on dispatch.

Acceptance

  • Enter during a turn adds an item and does not create a steer message.
  • Two items send in order, each after the previous turn completes.
  • After Stop the queue stays and sends nothing until Resume.
  • A docked request pauses dispatch; answering it resumes.
  • Reload restores the queue paused.
  • Alt+↑ on item 2 makes it item 1 and the order is used on dispatch.

Behavior

  • canSend = !!text.trim() && !busy && (!!session || !!agentId) && !uploading.
  • Stop (stopTurn()): if the goal is active, first thread/goal/set { status: "paused" }; then transport.interrupt(id). A 409 (turn already ended) is swallowed. Set stopping = true and the queue pause reason stopped.

Acceptance

  • Every row of the matrix can be reproduced and matches.
  • Stop during an active goal pauses the goal before the interrupt.
  • A 409 on interrupt shows no error.

Esc with focus inside a docked request card cancels that request (D-06), only after any menu inside it has closed. Esc in the textarea never cancels a request.

IME rules

  • Every key handler returns early when e.nativeEvent.isComposing is true or e.keyCode === 229. The second check covers Safari, which reports the confirming Enter with isComposing false and keyCode 229.
  • Track composition with compositionstart/compositionend in a ref. Do not recompute the slash or mention query during composition; recompute once on compositionend.
  • The Enter that ends a composition never sends, never completes a menu row and never queues.
  • The mention trigger also accepts the full-width at sign ＠ (U+FF20) proposal D-NEW-07. The slash menu only accepts ASCII /, matching parseChatInput.
  • The privacy scan debounce (250ms) and the placeholder logic ignore composition state; they read text only.
  • SmoothTextarea hides its custom caret during composition so the IME underline and candidate window line up with the native caret proposal D-NEW-12.

Accessibility summary

  • One polite live region inside the form (#composer-live, visually hidden) for queue, upload and menu counts. Alerts use role="alert" on the element itself (file errors, budget error, approval error).
  • Every icon-only control has an aria-label listed in its block. Minimum hit area 26×26, 34×34 for Send, Stop and Steer.
  • Focus return: popovers → their chip; menus keep focus in the textarea; removed chips → next chip or textarea; Stopping end → textarea.
  • Text under 13px uses --ink-2. This changes the slash description and project note from --ink-3.

Message stream

The message stream is everything inside the conversation scroller: user bubbles, grouped agent responses, the work each turn did, the answer and its rich parts. v3 keeps the entry reducers in lib/chat.ts and the grouping in ChatMessages. It adds message actions, a code block with controls, a folded work group that finally mounts RuntimeItem, an inline turn failure card, citations, file cards and tools for long chats.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §3. Target design: the stream boards in the v3 wireframe. Existing visual values come from truex-design-spec.html "4. Messages". Live requests (RequestCard, PlanApprovalCard, QuestionCard) and approval records (ApprovalRecordView) are specified in the Requests part. This part only fixes where they sit in a turn.

Rules for this part: text under 13px uses --ink-2. Filled buttons with light text use --accent-fg. Spacing, z-index and motion tokens (--sp-*, --z-*, --dur-*, --ease-*) come from the Foundations part. A turn means one user message plus every response group that shares its turnId. "Settled" means the turn is not active: !(running && isLastGroup).

      │   ├─ TurnFailureCard                failure for this turn         new, derive
      │   ├─ AnswerActions                  Copy · Regenerate · Branch · Restore
      │   ├─ TurnReceipt | LiveUsage                                      Observability part
      │   └─ SuggestedQuestions             last settled answer only      Composer part
      └─ StreamingPlaceholder               running, no response group yet
JumpToLatest pill                           sticky above the composer     new, derive

Data model

The persisted Message and the display Entry union stay the source for every row. New fields are optional, so today's history keeps rendering. Each new field names the backend item that supplies it. Fields tagged derive are computed on the client from data that exists today.

Entry union and Message

existsBE-03 BE-12 BE-13 BE-14 BE-15P1 shared/contracts.ts Message · lib/chat.ts Entry

The only structural change is two new entry kinds: failure (derive, P1) and file (BE-14, P3). Everything else is additive fields.

Data

// shared/contracts.ts
export interface Message {
  command?: CommandRecord;
  _id: string;
  sessionId: string;
  role: "user" | "assistant";
  text: string;
  at: string;
  turnId?: string;
  itemId?: string;
  clientId?: string;
  delivery?: "pending" | "accepted" | "failed" | "unknown";
  steer?: boolean;
  order?: number;
  messageIndex?: number;
  runtimeItemId?: string;
  // v3 additions
  citations?: Citation[];          // BE-13
  checkpointId?: string;           // BE-12, assistant only: snapshot taken before this turn
  mentions?: { kind: "agent" | "tool" | "file"; id: string; label: string }[]; // BE-15, user only
  editedFrom?: string;             // BE-03, user only: _id of the message this edit replaced
}

export interface Citation {        // BE-13
  index: number;                   // 1-based, matches [^n] in text
  title: string;                   // "IT handbook › Access requests"
  source: string;                  // connector or site label, e.g. "Google Drive"
  locator?: string;                // page, heading or line range
  url?: string;                    // http(s) only; anything else renders as plain text
}

// lib/chat.ts
export type Entry =
  | {
      kind: "message";
      command?: Message["command"];
      id: string;
      role: string;
      text: string;
      turnId?: string;
      itemId?: string;
      aliases?: string[];
      messageIndex?: number;
      final?: boolean;
      done?: boolean;
      delivery?: string;
      steer?: boolean;
      at?: string;                 // derive: copied from Message.at (history) or event time
      citations?: Citation[];      // BE-13
      checkpointId?: string;       // BE-12
      mentions?: Message["mentions"]; // BE-15
    }
  | { kind: "thinking"; id: string; turnId?: string; itemId?: string;
      text: string; summary?: string; raw?: string; done?: boolean }
  | { kind: "item"; id: string; turnId?: string; item: RuntimeItemData }  // typed, was any
  | { kind: "agents"; id: string; turnId?: string; threadIds: string[] }
  | { kind: "approval"; id: string; turnId?: string; record: ApprovalRecord }
  // new
  | { kind: "failure"; id: string;              // derive: "failure:{turnId|'none'}"
      turnId?: string; failure: TurnFailure; ref: ErrorRef; provider?: string }
  | { kind: "file"; id: string;                 // BE-14: "file:{file.id}"
      turnId: string; file: ConversationFile };

export interface RuntimeItemData {              // shapes RuntimeItem reads today
  id: string;
  type: "commandExecution" | "fileChange" | "mcpToolCall" | string;
  status?: string;                               // "inProgress" | "completed" | "failed" | other
  command?: string; aggregatedOutput?: string; exitCode?: number | null;
  changes?: { path: string; diff?: string; kind: unknown }[];
  server?: string; tool?: string;
  arguments?: unknown; result?: unknown;         // mcpToolCall payload, shown as JSON
  startedAt?: string; completedAt?: string;      // BE-04
}

export interface ConversationFile {              // shared/assistant-capabilities.ts
  id: string; name: string; size: number; createdAt: string; mediaType: string;
  sourceId?: string; kind?: "visualization"; title?: string; description?: string;
  mode?: "inline" | "wide";
  turnId?: string;                               // BE-14
  version?: number;                              // BE-14
}

Behavior

  • Entry id conventions stay: user clientId || itemId || _id; assistant answer:{turnId}:{itemId|messageIndex|listLength}; thinking thinking:{turnId}:{itemId|"default"}; item item:{turnId}:{item.id}; helpers agents:{turnId|"none"}; approval approval:{requestId}. New: failure:{turnId|"none"}, file:{id}.
  • Flags keep their meaning: final = text complete, done = turn completed, delivery and steer are user only.
  • An unknown citations index or a non-http url never throws. The chip renders as plain text.

Acceptance

  • History without any v3 field renders identically to today, apart from the new controls.
  • Entry has no any: item is RuntimeItemData.

Raw data to display pipeline

existsderiveP1 lib/chat.ts (reducers) · components/v2/chat-messages.tsx (grouping) · lib/stream-parts.ts (new, per-message parts)

Three stages. Reducers build Entry[] from history and events. Grouping turns entries into turns. The parts stage turns one assistant message's text into renderable parts. Stages 1 and 2 are pure and unit tested.

Data

// Stage 1: reducers (exist). All pure over Entry[].
historyEntries(messages: Message[]): Entry[]
upsertMessage(list, value): Entry[]            // identity merge, replay protection
mergeHistoryEntries(messages, live): Entry[]
addApprovals(list, records): Entry[]
addHelpers(list, turnId, threadIds): Entry[]
applyChatEvent(list, event: DomainEvent): Entry[]
visibleEntries(entries): Entry[]               // hides shadow streaming copies
// v3 additions (derive)
addFailure(list, turnId: string | undefined, failure: TurnFailure, ref: ErrorRef): Entry[]
clearFailure(list, turnId: string): Entry[]    // on retry or compact success
addFiles(list, files: ConversationFile[]): Entry[]   // BE-14, only files with turnId

// Stage 2: grouping (derive, replaces inline code in ChatMessages)
export interface Turn {
  key: string;                    // user entry id, or "turn:{turnId}" when no user entry
  turnId?: string;
  user?: Extract<Entry, { kind: "message" }>;
  groups: ResponseGroup[];        // usually 1
  active: boolean;                // running && last turn
  index: number;                  // 1-based, for outline and "Turn N"
}
export interface ResponseGroup {
  id: string; turnId?: string;
  thinking: Extract<Entry, { kind: "thinking" }>[];
  work: WorkEntry[];              // item + agents + approval, arrival order
  messages: Extract<Entry, { kind: "message" }>[];
  files: Extract<Entry, { kind: "file" }>[];
  failure?: Extract<Entry, { kind: "failure" }>;
}
type WorkEntry = Extract<Entry, { kind: "item" | "agents" | "approval" }>;
export function buildTurns(entries: Entry[], running: boolean): Turn[];

// Stage 3: per-message parts (derive)
export type StreamPart =
  | { type: "markdown"; text: string }
  | { type: "visualization"; id: string };
export function messageParts(text: string, streaming: boolean): {
  parts: StreamPart[];            // splitVisualizations(body, streaming)
  suggestions: string[];          // splitSuggestions(text, streaming)
  withheld: boolean;              // a partial [truex-visualization:… line was held back
};

Behavior

  • Stage 1 order is unchanged, including every applyChatEvent row in schema §3.1. kind:"item" entries are no longer dropped in grouping. They go to work.
  • Grouping: each user message starts a turn. Every other entry joins the previous non-user group with the same turnId, else starts a new response group. Thinking in a group merges into one ThinkingBlock (texts joined with \n\n).
  • Order inside a response group: meta, ThinkingBlock, WorkGroup, inline requests, answer messages, SourcesList, file cards, TurnFailureCard, AnswerActions, receipt, follow-ups.
  • Anchors: turn-{turnId} goes on the first response group of a turn. The usage receipt and AnswerActions go on its last group only.
  • addFailure places the entry by turnId. Source: the turn.completed or error event run through turnFailure(), with ErrorRef.turnId from the event. With no turnId it attaches to the latest turn. See TurnFailureCard.
  • Stage 3 order is fixed: splitSuggestions first, then splitVisualizations, then markdown. Both splitters are fence-aware (``` or ~~~, length-aware). CodeBlock and CitationChip run inside markdown, so a marker in a fence stays code.
  • Memoize buildTurns on entries and running, and messageParts per entry on text and streaming.

Acceptance

  • buildTurns puts a commandExecution item in work of its turn, not in a new group.
  • A [truex-visualization:<uuid>] line inside a code fence renders as code.
  • A late delta after message.final does not change text (replay protection kept).
  • A failure event with no turnId attaches to the last turn; with a turnId it attaches to that turn even if newer turns exist.

StateConditionOutputTag
Empty conversationpage emptyHero with composer, not ChatMessagesexists
Waiting for first outputrunning and last turn has no response groupStreamingPlaceholderexists
Thinking streamingactive, no answer text, some thinking not done"thinking…" meta + ThinkingBlock with spinnerexists

Visualization without sessionsessionId missing"Open this conversation to view the visualization."exists

Behavior

  • "Active" = running && turn is last. "Answering" = any message in the group has non-empty text.
  • Ordering is arrival order from the reducers. The component never sorts by time. Inline request cards render at the end of the work area of the turn that owns them (BE-02 turnId). Until then they render after the latest turn, as today.
  • Keys: turn key, group id, entry id. Never array index.
  • Rendering cost: settled turns are wrapped in React.memo keyed on their entries. Only the active turn re-renders on each delta.
  • Page wiring kept: onPrompt and onCommand fill the composer and focus it, they do not send. onSuggest sends. suggestionsEnabled = !busy && !goalMode && !failure && !pending.length.

Keyboard and a11y

  • The scroller keeps role=log, aria-label="Conversation", aria-live=off. Streaming text is not announced token by token.
  • A polite live region (#sm-live, .sr-only) announces once per turn: "{agentName} replied." when the answer goes final, "{agentName} stopped." on stop, and "{failure label}." on failure.
  • Each article keeps its aria-label: "Your message", "{agentName} response".

Acceptance

  • A 200-turn chat re-renders only the last turn per delta (React profiler).
  • The live region speaks once when an answer finishes, not per delta.
  • Runtime items render inside their turn's WorkGroup.

Auto-follow and turn anchors

existsP1 app/page.tsx .scroll follow logic → lib/use-stream-follow.ts (new hook, same rules)

Keeps the newest output in view while the reader is at the bottom, and stops as soon as they scroll away.

Data

export function useStreamFollow(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement>, deps: {
  entries: Entry[]; pending: PendingRequest[];
}): {
  following: boolean;
  missed: number;                   // entries added while not following (JumpToLatest)
  jump(): void;                     // scroll to bottom, following = true, missed = 0
  scrollToTurn(turnId: string): void;
};
export const FOLLOW_THRESHOLD = 80; // px, exists

Behavior

  • On scroll: following = scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight < 80. Unchanged.
  • When entries or pending change and following is true, jump to the bottom with behavior: "instant". Unchanged.
  • When not following, count new entries (by id, not by delta) into missed.
  • Sending a message always sets following to true and jumps.
  • Opening a WorkGroup, code block or visual above the viewport must not jump the reader. Use CSS overflow-anchor: auto on .scroll (browser default) and never call scroll from these toggles.
  • scrollToTurn: find #turn-{turnId}, set tabIndex=-1, scroll with block: "start" (smooth, instant with reduced motion), then focus with preventScroll. Used by the outline, search and the goal timeline.

Acceptance

  • Scrolling up 81px during streaming stops follow; the view does not move as text arrives.
  • Scrolling back within 80px of the bottom resumes follow.
  • Opening a folded group above the viewport keeps the visible text in place.

interface CodeBlockProps {

Behavior

  • Language label: lang as written, or "text" when missing.
  • Highlighting library proposal D-NEW-S5: shiki with the JS regex engine and a lazy-loaded grammar per language, run after the fence closes. Fallback when the grammar is unknown or loading fails: plain text. Blocks over 2000 lines skip highlighting.
  • Fence awareness: splitSuggestions and splitVisualizations run on the raw text first and already skip fenced lines (``` and ~~~, length-aware). CodeBlock only receives what markdown parsed as a fence, so a marker inside a fence is shown as code and never becomes a visual. Both splitters and the markdown parser must agree on fence rules: add a shared test fixture.
  • Copy copies code exactly, not the highlighted HTML and not only the visible lines.
  • Wrap and collapse state are per block and reset on reload.

Keyboard and a11y

  • pre is tabindex=0 with aria-label="{lang} code" so it scrolls with the keyboard. Wrap is aria-pressed. Expand button has aria-expanded.

Acceptance

  • A 31-line block shows 20 lines and "Show 11 more lines"; a 30-line block is not collapsed.
  • Copy on a collapsed block copies all 31 lines.
  • Syntax colors change with theme with no library theme CSS loaded.
  • A [truex-visualization:<uuid>] line inside ~~~ stays code.

interface WorkGroupProps {
  id: string;                 // "work:{groupId}"
  entries: WorkEntry[];       // arrival order
  active: boolean;
  older: boolean;             // not the latest turn
  open?: boolean; onToggle?: (open: boolean) => void;
  subAgents: SubAgentState; sessionId?: string;
  onOpenAgent?: (threadId: string) => void;
}
// summary: counts by type in this fixed order, joined with ", ", then " · {h} helper(s)"
//   mcpToolCall      → "called {n} tool(s)"
//   commandExecution → "ran {n} command(s)"
//   fileChange       → "edited {n} file(s)"   (n = distinct paths across changes)
//   approval         → "{n} approval(s)"
//   other            → "{n} step(s)"
// first letter capitalized. Example: "Called 3 tools, ran 1 command, edited 1 file · 2 helpers"

Behavior

  • Open by default while active. It folds 600ms after the turn settles, so the fold does not jump mid-read. proposal D-NEW-S6. With reduced motion it folds at once.
  • A reader's toggle beats the default for the rest of the page session.
  • The wireframe says "Read 3 docs". Tool verbs need a tool category that the data does not carry, so v3 says "called {n} tools". A verb map by tool name is D-NEW-S8.
  • Total time = last completedAt − first startedAt (BE-04). Hidden without BE-04. The receipt still shows turn time.
  • Search hits inside a folded group open it (see ThreadSearch).
  • Rows update live only with BE-04 item events. Without BE-04 the group fills from item.started and item.completed, as the reducer does today.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Toggle is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. The summary text is its accessible name. Nothing inside is announced live except a failed row, which announces "Command failed" or "Tool call failed".

Acceptance

  • A settled turn with 3 MCP calls, 1 command, 1 file edit and 2 helpers reads "Called 3 tools, ran 1 command, edited 1 file · 2 helpers".
  • An older group the reader opened stays open after new turns arrive.
  • A turn with no work entries shows no WorkGroup frame.

Data

export type ErrorReason =
  | "rateLimited" | "quota" | "credentials" | "providerDown" | "contextWindow" | "other";
export interface TurnFailure { reason: ErrorReason; message: string; httpStatus?: number }
export interface ErrorRef { code?: string; requestId?: string; turnId?: string }
turnFailure(error): TurnFailure                     // unknown reason → "other"
providerTip(provider: string, reason: ErrorReason): string | undefined
interface TurnFailureCardProps {
  failure: TurnFailure; ref: ErrorRef; provider?: string;
  canRetry: boolean;                 // !readOnly && !running
  onRetry?: () => void; onCompact?: () => void;
  resetAt?: string;                  // BE-21, rateLimited only
}
export const RETRY_ALLOWED: Record<ErrorReason, boolean> = {
  rateLimited: true, quota: false, credentials: false,
  providerDown: true, contextWindow: false, other: true,
};

Behavior

  • Placement: the failure entry for the turn's turnId (from the event or ErrorRef.turnId). With no turnId it attaches to the latest turn. A guaranteed turnId on every failure event is BE-NEW-S2.
  • Retry: with BE-05 it resumes the turn. Until then it resends the turn's user message text as a new message. Retry and Compact clear the card when the next turn starts (clearFailure).
  • A goal failure (goalFailure(status, failure), only while goal status is blocked or usageLimited) keeps showing in the GoalBar too. The action there is "Resume goal", not Retry.
  • The page error banner stays for page-level errors that have no turn (load, send, command). A turn failure no longer also shows the banner.
  • Stop by the person is not a failure: no card, see Partial answer.
  • Follow-ups are hidden while a failure is the latest turn state (!failure is already in suggestionsEnabled).

Keyboard and a11y

  • role=alert only for a failure that arrives live. Cards from history render with no role so reloads do not announce. The action button gets focus only if focus was in the stream.

Copy

"Retry", "Compact", "Reconnect {provider}" (BE-NEW-S1), rate-limit countdown "Retry in {m:ss}" (BE-21).

Acceptance

  • quota shows label, hint and the matching providerTip, and no Retry.
  • contextWindow shows Compact only.
  • other shows failure.message as the hint.
  • A failure for turn 5 renders in turn 5 when turn 6 exists.

Requests and Needs you

A request is anything the agent cannot continue without: a tool approval, a question or a plan review. Today one RequestCard per pending request renders after <ChatMessages> in .thread, so it scrolls with the transcript. v3 docks the head request above the composer, leaves a placeholder in the stream where the turn paused, and folds each answered request into an audit row. A topbar tray, Needs you, gathers every item blocking the chat with one fix per row. Two or more open requests can be reviewed in one sheet.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §3.0.3, §3.0.4, §3.5, §3.7 and §7.3.8. The answer helpers in §2.14 (lib/request-input.ts) are reused unchanged; their coverage row lives in the Composer part. Target design: design/.cv3-parts/requests.html. In this section page means Home in frontend/app/page.tsx, and pending means the page's list of open PendingRequests.

Hard facts that shape this part: buttons come only from options[] ({label, description}, no recommended flag). Plan approval is Approve or Revise. On expiry a non-secret question continues with its first option, while approvals and secret questions are declined. PendingRequest has no turnId, createdAt or threadId today (BE-02). Plans and secrets always ask, in every approval mode. Contrast: text under 13px uses --ink-2; filled buttons with light text use --accent-fg.

It is chosen when any question has kind === "toolApproval". The submit logic stays in one hook.
