Data

PendingRequest, ApprovalRecord and derived views

existsbackendP1 shared/contracts.ts · lib/request-input.ts · lib/approval-mode.ts · new lib/requests.ts (derive helpers)

The contract types stay as they are. BE-02 adds three optional fields to PendingRequest. Every rule below has a fallback for when they are absent, so P1 ships without them.

Data

// shared/contracts.ts (exists, BE-02 additions marked)
export interface PendingRequest {
  requestId: string;
  method: string;                  // only "item/tool/requestUserInput" is rendered
  detail: Record<string, unknown>; // detail.questions: InputQuestion[]
  expiresAt: string;               // ISO; unanswered requests auto-resolve
  responseSchema: string | null;   // always null publicly
  turnId?: string;                 // BE-02: turn that paused on this request
  createdAt?: string;              // BE-02: ISO, when the runtime raised it
  threadId?: string;               // BE-02: helper thread that asked (absent = main agent)
}
export interface InputOption { label: string; description?: string; }
export interface InputQuestion {
  id: string;
  kind?: "toolApproval";           // MCP tool permission prompt
  header?: string;                 // "Permission needed" for tool approvals
  question: string;
  action?: string;                 // humanised tool name, e.g. "Create sales order"
  isOther?: boolean;               // allows free text
  isSecret?: boolean;              // masked input; answer never echoed back
  options?: InputOption[] | null;
}

// shared/contracts.ts (exists, unchanged)
export interface ApprovalRecord {
  requestId: string;
  at?: string;
  turnId?: string;
  outcome: "answered" | "auto" | "expired" | "interrupted";
  autoMode?: "readOnly" | "auto" | "grant";
  items: (
    | { kind: "toolApproval"; action?: string;
        decision: "allowedOnce" | "allowedSession" | "allowedChat" | "allowedAlways"
                | "declined" | "expired" | "interrupted" }
    | { kind: "question"; question: string; answer?: string; note?: string; secret?: true }
  )[];
}

// Answer payload (exists) → POST /api/sessions/:id/approvals/:requestId { result }
type AnswerPayload = { answers: { [questionId: string]: { answers: string[] } } };
// plan: { answers: { plan_approval: { answers: ["Approve"] | ["Revise", "user_note: <feedback>"] } } }

// lib/requests.ts (new, derive)
export type RequestKind = "tool" | "question" | "plan";
export interface RequestView {
  request: PendingRequest;
  questions: InputQuestion[];      // detail.questions, [] if not an array
  kind: RequestKind;               // plan: single question id "plan_approval"; tool: any kind "toolApproval"
  secret: boolean;                 // any question.isSecret === true
  expiryOutcome: "declined" | { continuesWith: string } | "server";  // see Expiry rule
  orderKey: number;                // Date.parse(createdAt) if BE-02, else Date.parse(expiresAt)
  totalMs: number;                 // expiresAt − (createdAt ?? firstSeen), floor 1000
  anchorTurnId: string | null;     // turnId (BE-02) ?? seenTurn.get(requestId) ?? null
}
export function requestViews(pending: PendingRequest[], seen: SeenMaps): RequestView[]; // sorted
export function expiryOutcome(v: Omit<RequestView, "expiryOutcome">): RequestView["expiryOutcome"];

Behavior

  • detail.questions is unknown in the type. Parse it once in requestViews: keep entries with a string id and string question, drop the rest. A request with zero valid questions is not docked and not counted.
  • Sort order: orderKey ascending, then firstSeen ascending, then requestId. Until BE-02 the key is expiresAt, so the request that expires soonest leads. This is a stand-in for arrival order and is labelled "oldest first" only once createdAt exists. derive
  • expiryOutcome: kind === "tool" or secret → "declined". Otherwise, if the current question has options → { continuesWith: options[0].label }. Plan → { continuesWith: "Approve" }. A free-text-only question → "server" (copy stays generic). derive
  • msLeft(expiresAt, now) from lib/request-input.ts drives every countdown. Do not add a second timer.
  • firstSeen and seenTurn are filled on approval.requested and on history load. They are dropped when the request leaves pending. After a reload, firstSeen is the reload time, so the ring may start part-way: that is accepted until BE-02.

Acceptance

  • A request whose detail.questions is missing or not an array renders nothing and does not change the Needs-you count.
  • Two requests with expiresAt 10:30 and 10:25 dock the 10:25 one first. With BE-02 createdAt present, the earlier createdAt leads regardless of expiresAt.
  • The answer payload for a tool approval sends the original option label ("Allow"), never the display label ("Allow once").

Behavior

  • Stacking order: the dock shows views[0] (sorted by orderKey, see Data). Until BE-02 that is soonest expiresAt first. The count reads "{index+1} of {views.length}", where index is the head's position, always 1 outside the batch sheet. derive
  • New requests never replace the card the user is looking at. If a request arrives with a lower orderKey than the head while the head card has focus or a typed draft, it joins the queue behind it and the count grows. The order is applied again when focus leaves the card. proposal D-NEW: keep head stable
  • Height budget with the phone keyboard open (visualViewport.height < 0.75 × innerHeight, from the Shell part): the bottom bar hides. The budget is visualViewport.height − --topbar-h − composerHeight − 16. If the full card is taller than 0.45 × budget, render compact. Measure with ResizeObserver on the card and a visualViewport resize listener, throttled to one rAF. proposal D-NEW: dock height budget
  • Compact keeps the primary action live: for tool approvals the first option, for plans Approve, for questions "Show" only (options need room). Keys still work on a focused compact card.
  • The composer stays usable. Enter queues while the turn runs; the queue pauses with reason request (Composer part). Suggestions are hidden while a request is docked.
  • The stage's follow logic treats the dock as part of .bottom: its height is added to the scroll padding, so the last message is never hidden behind it.
  • Answers only happen in the dock or the batch sheet. The anchor and tray rows focus the dock; they never render controls.

Keyboard and a11y

  • div.request-dock[role=region][aria-label="Needs your answer"]. The card form keeps aria-labelledby its h3.
  • Focus is never moved into the dock on arrival. The user reaches it with Shift+Tab from the composer, the anchor's "Answer" link, the tray or g n.
  • Answer keys fire only while focus is inside the card, never from the composer textarea (see each card).

Acceptance

  • With one pending request, the card sits between the error banner slot and HelperChip, and scrolling the stream does not move it.
  • With three pending, the head card shows "1 of 3" and the batch bar reads "3 pending".
  • At 390×844 with the keyboard open, the dock and the composer are both fully visible; a tall plan card renders compact with Approve visible.
  • A second request arriving while the user types in the head card's text field does not replace the card.
  • The last message stays visible above the dock at the bottom of the stream.

RequestAnchor (stream placeholder)

derivebackendP1 components/v2/request-anchor.tsx (new) · rendered by ChatMessages

A dashed row in the stream at the point where the turn paused, so the transcript shows why it stopped. It links to the docked card and disappears when the request resolves; the audit row takes its place.

Waiting for your permission · Example: Run a shell commandAnswer ↓

Anatomy and sizes

row
flex, gap --sp-2, wrap, padding 7px 10px, radius --r-ctl, 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn) 55%, transparent), background color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn-bg) 55%, transparent), 12.5 --warning-text

Behavior

  • Without BE-02: the anchor goes at the end of the entry list, after the live turn's last entry. If seenTurn recorded a turn id and that turn is still the last turn, it goes at the end of that turn (same place). If the user has sent more messages since, it stays after the recorded turn's last entry. If no turn id was seen (loaded from history), it goes at the very end. derive
  • With BE-02 turnId: the anchor goes inside that turn, after the entry whose turnId matches and that was last before the request (the running tool step, when the Stream part renders steps). Several anchors in one turn stack in orderKey order. backend BE-02
  • With BE-02 threadId for a helper: the anchor is also placed in that helper's group, kind phrase "{helperName} is waiting for your permission". Until then, never name a helper. backend BE-02, D-07
  • "Answer" focuses the docked card's first control. If the request is not the head (behind others), it opens the batch sheet at that request.
  • On approval.resolved the anchor is removed in the same render that inserts the audit row, so the stream does not jump.

Keyboard and a11y

  • div.request-anchor[role=note]. Button name "Answer: {title}".
  • Not a live region; the dock arrival is announced once (see Timing).

  • Without turnId, the anchor renders after the last entry of the turn that was live when the request arrived.

Request cards

All three cards share today's internals: useExpiry(expiresAt) on the shared 1s clock (useClock), answerErrorMessage for send errors, and p.request-error[role=alert] + <ErrorRef> for failures. v3 moves submit state into one hook so the dock, the compact form and the batch sheet share it.

// components/v2/use-request-answer.ts (new, derive)
function useRequestAnswer(view: RequestView, onAnswer: (value: unknown) => Promise<void>): {
  sending: string | null;          // label of the pressed button, or null
  error: { message: string; ref?: ErrorRefData } | null;
  locked: boolean;                 // sending || expired || frozen || readOnly
  submit(payload: AnswerPayload, pressed: string): Promise<void>;
};
// submit: guards double-press (sending !== null → no-op), calls onAnswer,
// on reject sets error = answerErrorMessage(status). 409/404/410 also mark the
// request as gone: the card hides after 2000ms if approval.resolved has not arrived.

Shows the time left before the request auto-resolves and what will happen then. Today it is text only: "Expires in {LiveDuration trend=-1}". v3 adds a ring and a consequence line.

Anatomy and sizes

ring
32×32, 3px stroke via conic-gradient(var(--warn) calc(var(--p) * 1%), var(--surface-3) 0) with a 26px --surface inner disc; --accent instead of --warn for questions and plans

States

StateTriggerVisualCopy
CountingmsLeft > 60000ring fill --p = msLeft / totalMs × 100tool/secret: "then declined"; others: none (rule line in the card)
Last minutemsLeft ≤ 60000time turns --warning-textsame
ExpiredmsLeft === 0ring hidden; card locksper card, see below

Behavior

  • totalMs = expiresAt − createdAt (BE-02), else expiresAt − firstSeen. Floor 1000ms. The ring is decorative; the time text is the source of truth. derive
  • Ticks on useClock(!expired). No per-card setInterval.
  • Expiry is decided by the server. The client locks at 0 and waits for approval.resolved; it never sends an answer on the user's behalf.
  • Reduced motion: the ring updates in steps with no transition (it has none by default).

Keyboard and a11y

  • Ring aria-hidden. Visible text wrapped in span.sr-only "Expires in {m} minutes {s} seconds" that updates only at 60s, 30s and 10s left (see Timing), not every tick.

Acceptance

  • A request with 90s left shows "1:30" and a ring at about 75% if it arrived 30s ago.
  • The countdown text changes every second; the screen reader hears at most three countdown messages.
  • At 0 the card locks and no network request is sent.

Behavior

  • The first-option marker and the rule describe the server's expiry behavior. Never label any option "Recommended"; the contract has no such flag.

  • Esc (D-06): a question has no Cancel option, so Esc in the card moves focus to the composer without answering. If the Other input is open and empty, Esc first closes it. proposal D-06
  • Option buttons use aria-pressed; the group has aria-labelledby the legend. The rule line is in aria-describedby of the fieldset.

Plan approvals arrive as question items: answer "Approve", or "Revise" with the feedback in note.

Footer (recordSummary) "{summary} at {h:mm}": answered → "You answered"; auto → autoModeLabel or "Recommended option chosen"; expired / interrupted → "Closed". Omitted when at is missing or invalid.

Behavior

  • Placement: where the request's anchor was. In history (no anchor), after the entry of the same turnId when present, else in arrival order (today's rule).
  • One record can hold several items (multi-question requests); each item is one row, in array order.
  • Records are never collapsed or grouped with neighbours. Consecutive auto records (Autopilot) stay separate so each decision is traceable.
  • Answer and note text render as plain text, never markdown or HTML.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Not focusable. role=group "Your decision"; the dot is aria-hidden, so tone is carried by the badge text.
  • time carries the ISO at in dateTime.

Acceptance

  • Every cell of the tool-decision table above renders its label and tone.
  • A secret item renders "Answer hidden" even if a stale answer string is present in the payload.
  • A record without at renders no footer.
  • outcome:"auto", autoMode:"readOnly", decision:"declined" renders "Not allowed".

// lib/needs-you.ts (new, derive)
export type NeedsItem =
  | { kind: "request"; id: string; view: RequestView }                  // exists data
  | { kind: "goal"; id: "goal"; goal: Goal; failure?: TurnFailure }     // exists data
  | { kind: "helper"; id: string; agent: SubAgent }                     // status errored | notFound
  | { kind: "mcp"; id: string; name: string };                          // BE-06 authRequired

export function needsYou(input: {
  views: RequestView[];
  goal: Goal | null;
  goalStoppedByUser: boolean;      // client flag: Stop paused the goal in this tab
  failure: TurnFailure | null;
  helpers: SubAgent[];
  mcp: Record<string, { authRequired: boolean }>;   // BE-06, {} until then
  firstSeen: Map<string, number>; // per item id, set when the item first qualifies
}): NeedsItem[];

Behavior

  • Aggregation: one row per request, at most one goal row (the most specific row above wins: context window, then status), one per qualifying helper, one per MCP server. The count is needsYou(...).length, shown by the Shell part's button.
  • Order: requests first, in RequestView order. Then goal, helpers and MCP rows in firstSeen order. Head label: "soonest first" until BE-02, "oldest first" with createdAt. derive
  • The Shell part also lists the last turn failure as a count input. Turn failures without a goal already show in the stream's error banner, so the tray shows a failure only through the goal context-window row. proposal D-NEW: turn failure in Needs you
  • Rows leave when their source clears: request resolved, goal status changes, helper dismissed, MCP signed in. A helper row is dismissed when its fix runs or the user presses the row's close (×, 24×24, "Dismiss").
  • After a fix runs, the tray stays open if rows remain and moves focus to the next row; it closes when empty. Fix errors show inline under the row as 12 --bad text.
  • While turn.frozen, rows and count hold their last values and fix buttons are disabled.
  • Until BE-06, MCP rows never appear. Never infer sign-in state from other errors.

Keyboard and a11y

  • g then n (second key within 1000ms, not in an input, textarea, select or contenteditable): opens the tray and focuses the first row. If the tray is empty, nothing opens and "Nothing needs you right now." is announced. proposal D-NEW-7 (Shell part)
  • Rows are a role=list; each row is role=listitem containing its fix button. ↑/↓ move between rows (roving tabindex on the fix buttons), Home/End jump, Enter runs the fix, Esc closes and returns focus to the count button.
  • Fix button names include the row: "Review: {title}", "Sign in to {name}".

Acceptance

  • Two requests, a budgetLimited goal and a notFound helper give a count of 4, with the requests first.
  • A goal that is blocked with a contextWindow failure shows one goal row with "Compact conversation".
  • Pressing g then n in the stage opens the tray with the first row focused; typing "gn" in the composer does nothing.
  • "Review" on a request closes the tray and focuses the docked card; no second answer UI appears in the tray.
  • Without BE-06 no MCP row ever renders.

BatchBar and BatchReviewSheet

deriveP2 components/v2/batch-review.tsx (new) · uses Sheet (Shell part)

With two or more open requests, a bar above the docked card offers "Review all", which opens a sheet that steps through every request in order. Each step renders the same card body, so rules and keys are identical.

Read-only viewer

Read-only viewer: "Waiting on owner"

backendP2 RequestDock, RequestAnchor, NeedsYouTray with readOnly = viewer is not the owner

Only the owner can write. A viewer of a shared chat sees that the chat is paused on a person, but never gets answer controls. Knowing the owner's name and that the viewer is not the owner needs BE-09 (ownerName, viewer rules).

Behavior

  • Until BE-09 there is no way to tell a viewer from the owner, so this state is not built in P1. Fallback copy when ownerName is missing: "Waiting on the owner".
  • The viewer's composer is replaced by the viewer bar (States part), so no answer path exists anywhere on the page.
  • If a viewer POSTs anyway, the server's 403 renders the generic answerErrorMessage fallback; the client never shows controls, so this is only a guard.

Keyboard and a11y

  • The viewer dock is role=status with text "Waiting on {ownerName} to answer: {title}". Not focusable.

Acceptance

  • As a viewer, no button, input or key handler exists inside the dock.
  • A viewer sees "Answer hidden" for secret items and "{ownerName} answered" in the footer.

Reduced motion: all --dur-* are 0s (Foundations), so the dock and tray appear instantly. The delays above (400ms, 600ms, 2000ms) are not motion and still apply.

Focus management

  • A new request never steals focus. The user may be typing in the composer.
  • After an answer from the dock: if another request docks, focus moves to its first control. Otherwise focus moves to the composer textarea.
  • If focus was inside a card that disappears for any other reason (expired and resolved, answered in another tab), move focus to the composer only if focus would otherwise fall to body.
  • Multi-question step change: focus the new fieldset (tabIndex=-1), as today.
  • Revise: focus the textarea on open; Cancel returns focus to "Revise".
  • Tray: opening focuses the first row's fix button. Esc returns focus to the count button. A fix that moves focus elsewhere (dock, composer) closes the tray first.
  • Batch sheet: focus is trapped. Close returns focus to "Review all", or to the composer if the bar is gone.
  • The anchor's "Answer" and g n scroll the dock into view with block: "nearest" before focusing.

Agents, helpers and goals

Everything that works on the user's behalf. The goal strip leads with checkpoint progress, then the token budget, and every stop names one fix. Helpers appear as one "Handed off" node per turn in the stream and as a roster in the Agents tab. Persistent agents get an All agents sheet and the existing create dialog. MCP servers get a tools shelf that finally shows scope, warnings and shadowing, which the API already returns.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §4 (Goals) and §5 (Agents, Subagents, Tools and MCP). Target design: the agents boards in the v3 wireframe (design/.cv3-parts/agents.html). Existing visual values: truex-design-spec.html sections Goal tab, Agents tab, Agents roster and New agent dialog. The turn state and the status pill are defined once in Shell (deriveTurnState(), see Topbar); this part only reads them.

Terms. Agent is a persistent specialist stored per tenant (Agent / AgentSummary), mentioned as @handle. Helper is a sub-agent the main agent spawns inside one session (SubAgent). Connected tools are MCP servers attached to an agent. Spacing, z-index and motion tokens (--sp-*, --z-*, --dur-*, --ease-*) come from Foundations. Today's CSS uses --success-bg/--success-text and --warning-bg/--warning-text; this spec names them by their shell equivalents --ok-bg/--ok and --warn-bg/--warn-text at the same values.

Goal data and status

Goal data model and status table

existsP1 shared/contracts.ts · frontend/lib/goal.ts · frontend/lib/goal-errors.ts · shared/errors.ts

One goal per conversation. The Codex runtime works toward it across turns until it is complete, paused, stopped by an error or out of token budget. The assistant marks it complete; the user then accepts it or reopens it with feedback. All types below exist unless tagged.

Data

export type GoalStatus =
  | "active" | "paused" | "blocked" | "usageLimited" | "budgetLimited" | "complete";

export interface Goal {                 // runtime projection
  objective: string;
  status: GoalStatus;
  tokenBudget: number | null;
  tokensUsed: number;                   // Codex count, enforces the budget
  timeUsedSeconds: number;
  createdAt: number | null;             // identifies the goal; objective edits keep it
  updatedAt: number | null;
  tokensObserved?: number;              // Truex count; UI total = max of the two
  usageResetsAt?: string;               // BE-21: ISO time the usage limit resets
}

export interface SessionGoal {          // on Session, for the conversation list
  objective: string; status: GoalStatus; updatedAt?: string;
  createdAt?: number | null; tokensObserved?: number; tokenBudget?: number | null;
  goalUpdatedAt?: number | null; goalEventAt?: string;
}

export interface GoalHistoryEntry {
  at: string;
  kind: "set" | "objective" | "budget" | "status" | "accepted" | "reopened" | "cleared";
  objective: string;
  status?: GoalStatus; tokens?: number; tokenBudget?: number | null;
  feedback?: string; turnId?: string; tokensUsed?: number;
}

export interface GoalReview {
  objective: string; goalCreatedAt: number | null;
  decision: "accepted" | "reopened"; feedback?: string; at: string;
}

// Session fields
goal?: SessionGoal;
goalReview?: GoalReview;
goalCleared?: { createdAt: number | null; eventAt?: string }; // blocks replayed older updates
goalHistory?: GoalHistoryEntry[];                              // server keeps last 60

export type ErrorReason =
  | "rateLimited" | "quota" | "credentials" | "providerDown" | "contextWindow" | "other";
export interface TurnFailure { reason: ErrorReason; message: string; httpStatus?: number; }

// Live events: "goal.updated" { goal } and "goal.cleared".

// v3 derived view (new lib/goal-view.ts, derive)
export type GoalView =
  | "active" | "working" | "pausing" | "paused" | "blocked" | "usageLimited"
  | "budgetLimited" | "review" | "accepted";
export function goalView(goal: Goal, review: GoalReview | null, running: boolean): GoalView;

Codex-token note

The meter follows Codex tokensUsed, which runs lower than the Truex total. The meta title and the budget panel say so. Title with a budget: "{tokensUsed} of {tokenBudget} budget tokens used ({total} in total). The budget counts the runtime's tokens, which run lower than the total. The runtime enforces the stop."

Data

interface GoalStripView {
  objective: string;
  checkpoints: { done: number; total: number } | null; // derive: latest PlanStep[] of the session
  used: number | null;           // round(tokensUsed / tokenBudget * 100), cap 100; null without budget
  meterTone: "ok" | "warn" | "full";   // warn when used > 80, full at 100
  meta: string;
  pill: { cls: "s-running" | "s-paused" | "s-done" | "s-ended"; label: string; hint: string };
  view: GoalView;
}

Behavior

  • Checkpoints source: the plan the Goal tab already receives (latest PlanStep[]). done = steps with status completed; complete goal shows total/total. proposal D-NEW-AG-01
  • Meter updates on every goal.updated; it never animates backward except after Extend or Set budget.
  • Pause label is "Pause after this turn" when running, else "Pause goal". Pause shows only for active, Resume only for paused.
  • The "turn N" counter counts turns seen while mounted and appears from 2. It restarts on reload (known gap).
  • Clear always confirms: "Clear this goal? Its progress will no longer be tracked."
  • The status pill in the topbar (Shell) reads "working on goal" from deriveTurnState(); the strip does not duplicate the turn spinner.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Region: role="region", aria-label="Goal". Focus order: objective (not focusable), Pause/Resume, More, Clear, then stop-block buttons.
  • Meter: role="progressbar", aria-label="Token budget used", aria-valuenow 0-100, aria-valuetext "{used} of {budget} tokens".
  • Checkpoints: dots aria-hidden; text has aria-label "{done} of {total} checkpoints done".
  • Status changes announce once through a polite live region: "Goal {label}". Token-only updates stay silent.
  • Icon buttons carry their visible labels as aria-label: "Pause goal" / "Pause after this turn", "Resume goal", "Goal menu", "Clear goal".

Copy

fix
"Provide input", "Wait for reset", "Resets at {h:mm}", "Extend 25k", "Extend 50k", "Compact", "Resume goal", "Set budget"
run row
"Working on the goal[ · turn N]. Stop pauses it now.", "Pause after this turn", "Pausing after this turn. The assistant finishes its current step, then stops.", "Keep going"

Acceptance

  • With a 4-step plan and 2 done, the strip reads "2/4" before the budget meter.
  • At 41k of 50k the fill is --warn; at 40k it is --accent.
  • Each stop state shows exactly one solid button.
  • Extend 50k on a 50k budget with 50k used sets tokenBudget 100k and status active in one call.
  • With no budget, no meter renders and meta shows "{duration} · {total} tokens".
  • The meta title explains that the budget counts the runtime's tokens.

BudgetField props: { initial: number | null; onChange: (v: BudgetValue) => void;
  selectClassName?: string; showError?: boolean /* true */; autoFocus?: boolean /* false */ }

Behavior

  • Session open: goal = snapshot.goal, goalReview = data.goalReview. goal.updated sets goal and syncs the sidebar; goal.cleared clears goal and review.
  • Goal-mode submit: blocks with budgetHelp when invalid; confirms "Replace the current goal with this one?" unless complete; clears then sets. A goal can open a new conversation, whose title is the objective.
  • Stop while active sets paused first. Tooltip "Pause the goal and stop the current response".
  • BudgetField: select (sr-only label "Budget") with presets and "Custom…"; custom input aria-label="Custom token budget", placeholder "e.g. 50k", aria-invalid once touched. Reports its start value on mount.
  • Toasts: "Goal set.", "Goal updated.", "Goal paused.", "Goal resumed.", "Goal cleared.", "Token budget set to N." Usage error: "Usage: /goal budget <tokens>, for example /goal budget 50k".

Acceptance

  • Submitting a goal with budget "abc" shows budgetHelp and sends nothing.
  • Replacing a complete goal skips the confirm.

Goal commands in the transcript

existsP1 components/chat-messages.tsx (goal-tag) · components/command-result.tsx (CommandResult)

A user message carrying a thread/goal/* command shows span.goal-tag (target icon, "Goal") above the bubble. CommandResult shows the objective (or "Goal cleared." / "No goal is set."), a status label that follows live state when sameGoal(recorded, currentGoal), else the recorded status, and a dl of time, tokens (goalTokens) and budget.

Follow-ups "Check goal status" (/goal show) and a clear action (/goal clear) fill the composer, never send. Chat turn groups carry id="turn-{turnId}" on their first response for "View turn". Message rendering is owned by Stream.

Acceptance

  • An old /goal card for a replaced goal keeps its recorded status.

Agents are stored per tenant. The browser only ever sees AgentSummary, ModelOption and MCP summaries, never model profiles or keys.

Data

export interface Agent {                 // server shape
  _id: string; name: string; description: string; modelProfileId: string;
  systemPrompt: string; persona?: string; scope?: "business" | "general";
  sandbox: SandboxMode; approvalPolicy: AskForApproval;
  mcpProfileIds: string[]; skillIds?: string[];
  handle?: string;                       // no "@", unique per tenant
  look?: number;                         // 0 to AGENT_LOOK_COUNT - 1
  tint?: AgentTint; builtin?: boolean;   // builtin never set through the API
}
export const AGENT_TINTS = ["ice", "mint", "butter", "peach", "lilac"] as const;
export const AGENT_LOOK_COUNT = 12;
export const DEFAULT_AGENT_LOOK = 2;     // "Navy"
export const DEFAULT_AGENT_TINT = "ice";
export const AGENT_NAME_MAX = 40;
export const AGENT_PURPOSE_MAX = 80;
export const AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_MAX = 20000;
export function agentHandle(name: string): string {
  return name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "").slice(0, 20);
}

export interface AgentSummary {          // GET /api/agents, page `agents` state
  id: string; name: string; description: string;
  provider: string; model: string; sandbox: string;
  handle?: string; look: number; tint: AgentTint; builtin: boolean;
  approvalPolicy?: string;               // BE-NEW: roster facts (see New backend items)
  mcpCount?: number;                     // BE-NEW: roster facts
  starterPrompts?: string[];             // BE-18
  ownerId?: string;                      // BE-07: who may edit or delete
}
export interface ModelOption { id: string; name: string; provider: string; }

// lib/agents.ts
export function modelShort(name: string): string;  // "Claude Opus 5.5" → "opus 5.5"
export interface AgentFields { name: string; description: string; systemPrompt: string;
  look: number; tint: AgentTint; modelProfileId: string; }
export function createAgentBody(f: AgentFields): AgentFields;   // trims text fields
export function handleTaken(handle: string, agents: AgentSummary[]): boolean;
export const fetchModels = () => api("/api/models");            // GET
export const createAgent = (b: AgentFields) => api("/api/agents", b); // POST
export const updateAgent = (id: string, b: Partial<AgentFields>) =>   // BE-07
  api(`/api/agents/${id}`, b, "PATCH");
export const deleteAgent = (id: string) => api(`/api/agents/${id}`, undefined, "DELETE"); // BE-07

// lib/agent-look.ts
export interface Look { name: string; body: string; visor: string; glow: string;
  face: "line" | "eyes" | "happy"; acc?: string; accColor?: string; }
export interface Tint { id: AgentTint; label: string; bg: string; dot: string; }
export const tintOf = (id?: string): Tint;   // falls back to TINTS[0]
export const lookOf = (i?: number): Look;    // falls back to LOOKS[0]
export const tone = (hex: string, amt: number): string;
export const CONFETTI_COLORS = ["#3691CD","#BCDEE8","#A9D5BE","#EBCB8B","#F0B999","#C4BDE3","#F2C94C"];

api(path, body?) sends POST with a body and GET without. v3 adds an optional method argument for PATCH and DELETE BE-07.

Server defaults for POST /api/agents: _id: "agent_" + uuid, sandbox: "read-only", approvalPolicy: "on-request", mcpProfileIds: [], skillIds: [], builtin: false, enabled: true. The body accepts only name, description, systemPrompt, look, tint, modelProfileId; unknown fields are rejected.

Confetti

existsP1 components/v2/agent-badge.tsx (Confetti)

A burst when an agent is created. No props. 56 memoised pieces: random angle, distance 110-330px, spin ±360deg, every third piece a 7px dot, others 5-9 by 3-12px rects, delay 0-140ms, duration 1500-2400ms, colour cycling CONFETTI_COLORS. Values pass as CSS vars --x --y --r --c --w --h --d --t; @keyframes burst flings then falls 170px and fades. aria-hidden.

Acceptance

  • With reduced motion, no confetti renders.
  • Confetti never blocks clicks (pointer-events:none).

Behavior

  • Every open: reset form, GET /api/models, auto-select the first model, focus Name after 30ms.

  • Success step: heading receives the announcement through aria-live=polite; "Say hi" autofocused.

Acceptance

  • Typing "Research Scout" when @researchscout exists disables Create and shows the taken hint.

  • POST body has exactly six keys.
  • With BE-07 missing, no Edit or Remove control renders anywhere.
  • After a successful PATCH, the roster and dock show the new name without a reload.

Helpers (sub-agents)

lib/subagents.ts: state, status, naming and delegation

existsP1 frontend/lib/subagents.ts · shared/contracts.ts (SubAgent)

The one reducer and helper library every helper surface reads: the Handed off node, HelperGroup, HelperChip, the Agents tab and the tiled view.

Data

export type SubAgentStatus =
  | "pendingInit" | "running" | "interrupted" | "completed"
  | "errored" | "shutdown" | "notFound";
export interface SubAgent {
  threadId: string; path: string | null; nickname: string | null; role: string | null;
  depth: number;                 // 1 = spawned by main agent; >1 nested ("level N")
  status: SubAgentStatus; task?: string; lastMessage?: string;
  startedAt: string; endedAt?: string;              // ISO, server clock
  parentThreadId?: string;       // BE-08: exact delegation tree
  helperId?: string;             // BE-08: stable identity across resumes
  usage?: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; costUsd?: number }; // BE-08 (+ BE-11 currency)
  turnId?: string;               // BE-08: turn that spawned it
}
export interface SubAgentTranscript { agent: SubAgent; messages: { id: string; text: string; final: boolean }[]; }
export type CollabTool = "spawnAgent" | "sendInput" | "resumeAgent" | "wait" | "closeAgent";
export interface SubAgentState { agents: SubAgent[]; previews: Record<string, string>; skewMs?: number; }
export const emptySubAgents: SubAgentState = { agents: [], previews: {} };
export const PREVIEW_LIMIT = 4000;
export const TITLE_LIMIT = 48;
export const isRunning = (a: SubAgent) => a.status === "running" || a.status === "pendingInit";
export const statusLabels: Record<SubAgentStatus, string> = {
  pendingInit: "Starting", running: "Running", interrupted: "Stopped", completed: "Finished",
  errored: "Failed", shutdown: "Closed", notFound: "Unavailable",
};
// v3 derive: one tone function shared by every chip
export type HelperTone = "running" | "done" | "stopped" | "warn";
export function helperTone(s: SubAgentStatus | string): HelperTone;

export type DelegationMode = "explicitRequestOnly" | "proactive";
export interface DelegationPrefs { mode: DelegationMode; maxConcurrent: number; } // 1–5
export const defaultDelegation = { mode: "explicitRequestOnly", maxConcurrent: 3 };

Status: 7 values in 4 tones

◌ Starting◌ RunningFinishedStoppedClosed⚠ Failed⚠ Unavailable
statuslabeltonechip classextracolorsterminal
pendingInitStartingrunningis-runningspinner--accent-soft / --accent-fgno
runningRunningrunningis-runningspinner--accent-soft / --accent-fgno
completedFinisheddoneis-done–--ok-bg / --okyes
interruptedStoppedstoppedis-stopped–--surface-3 / --ink-2yes
shutdownClosedstoppedis-stopped–--surface-3 / --ink-2yes
erroredFailedwarnis-warn⚠--warn-bg / --warn-textyes
notFoundUnavailablewarnis-warn⚠--warn-bg / --warn-textyes
unknown stringraw status textstoppedis-stopped–as stoppedyes

Stopped chips use --ink-2 text, not today's --ink-3, because the chip text is 11px (contrast rule). There is no "Limited access" status.

Helper tones (identity color)

Separate from status tone. .tone-N with N = spawn index % 3 sets --t and --ts: tone-0 --t0/--ts0, tone-1 --t1/--ts1, tone-2 --t2/--ts2, main agent --tm/--tsm. Nested helpers inherit their parent's tone when parentThreadId exists (BE-08); until then they use their own index.

Behavior

  • applySubAgentEvent: snapshot sets membership; subagent.spawned|status|completed upsert d.agent; subagent.event kind message.delta appends to the preview (kept to 4000 chars), message.final sets lastMessage and replaces the preview, turn.started clears the preview. Finished helpers never revert to running. Clock skew learned from event at; samples over 10 minutes are ignored.
  • Naming helperName: nickname, else capitalised role (skips "default"), else "Helper N" by spawn order. Nested helpers show "{parent} › {name}" in the Handed off node only when parentThreadId exists (BE-08).
  • taskTitle(task): first sentence, clipped at a word boundary to 48 chars + "…"; empty → "Working on a task".
  • previewTail(text, maxChars = 240, maxLines = 4): markdown-balanced tail prefixed "…".
  • formatDuration (lib/observability): "0:38", "1:02:03".
  • Delegation: see DelegationSettings.

Acceptance

  • helperTone maps all 7 statuses as in the table and an unknown string to stopped.
  • A subagent.status running event after completed leaves the helper completed.
  • A helper with nickname null and role "default" is named "Helper 2" when it spawned second.

Data

interface HandoffNodeProps {
  id: string;                       // entry id
  threadIds: string[];              // entry.threadIds from the "agents" entry
  state: SubAgentState;
  delegation?: { mode: DelegationMode; maxConcurrent: number; source: "session" | "browser" };
                                    // session = BE-10 Session.delegation; browser = DelegationPrefs
  sessionId?: string;
  onOpenAgent: (threadId: string) => void;   // opens Agents tab detail
}

Behavior

  • Delegation label: "Only when I ask" for explicitRequestOnly, "Whenever it helps" for proactive. With BE-10 the label shows the session's stored mode; without it, the browser prefs are what the next chat will use, not what this chat used, so the pill is hidden for sessions created before the prefs last changed proposal D-NEW-AG-09.
  • Ordering: spawn order; with BE-08, depth-first under each parent.
  • Elapsed = (endedAt ?? now + skewMs) - startedAt, formatted with formatDuration.
  • "Open in panel" and a click on the avatar call onOpenAgent, which opens the Agents tab, opens that helper's detail and focuses #agent-card-{threadId} first when the detail closes.
  • When 2 or more helpers run at once, the tiled view renders under the tree.

Keyboard and a11y

  • section[aria-label="Helper agents"], tabIndex=-1 (HelperChip "View" scrolls and focuses it). Rows are buttons with aria-expanded.
  • Polite live region announces the summary on change only: "{n} helpers, {r} running". Timers are silent.
  • "level N" is text, so screen readers read nesting.

Acceptance

  • Three helpers in one turn render one node, not three.
  • A depth-3 helper indents 60px and shows "level 3".
  • All 7 statuses render with the right tone.
  • The delegation pill reads the session value once BE-10 ships.

BE-08P2 SubAgent.usage (BE-08) · currency via BE-11 · shown in Agents tab rows, detail stats and panel foot

SubAgent has no usage today, so helpers show elapsed time only. With BE-08 each helper carries its tokens, and with BE-11 its cost in currency.

Behavior

Connected tools (MCP)

McpSettings and the tools shelf

existsderiveBE-06P2 components/mcp-settings.tsx · Sheet panel "mcp" "Connected tools" in app/page.tsx · app/panels.css .mcp-*

Attach MCP servers to the current agent, add user servers and, new in v3, see who owns each one, whether it is safe and whether chats will actually use it. The API already returns scope, editable, shadowed, warnings, urlHost, hasKey and tenantProfiles; today's UI drops them. Edit and delete use the existing PATCH/DELETE /api/mcp/:id. Live status and OAuth wait on BE-06.

Data

type McpSummary = {
  id: string;                  // "mcp_" + uuid
  name: string;
  scope: "user" | "tenant";    // user = owned by one user; tenant = shared, admin-managed
  enabled: boolean;            // false → "unavailable"
  transport: string;           // "http" or "configured" (legacy)
  hasKey: boolean;             // value never returned
  urlHost?: string;            // host[:port] only
  agentIds: string[];
  warnings?: string[];
};
type AgentMcpResponse = {
  profileIds: string[];
  profiles: (McpSummary & { editable: boolean; shadowed?: true; attached: boolean })[];
  tenantProfiles: (McpSummary & { editable: boolean; attached: true })[];   // read-only
};
// GET /api/mcp → { userProfiles, tenantProfiles }
type McpAuth = { kind: "none" | "bearer" | "header"; headerName?: string };  // + write-only apiKey

// BE-06: live status, from the "mcp.status" domain event
type McpStatus = { id: string; state: "connected" | "connecting" | "error" | "disconnected";
  toolCount?: number; authRequired?: boolean; message?: string };

// v3 component state (derive)
type Row = AgentMcpResponse["profiles"][number] & { status?: McpStatus };
// profiles: Row[]; tenant: Row[]; selected: string[]; ready; busy; error; notice;
// editing: string | null; confirmDelete: string | null; tab: "yours" | "workspace";
// tenantDenied: boolean   // GET /api/tenant/mcp returned 403

Validation (add and edit)

FieldRules
Namerequired, maxLength 64, placeholder "sap-tools". v3 client pattern matches the server: /^[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:_[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*$/; message "MCP name must be 1–64 letters, digits or hyphens, with single underscores between words"
Endpoint URLrequired on create, type=url, placeholder "https://example.com/mcp"; http allowed; show the plain-HTTP warning inline as soon as the URL starts with http://
AuthenticationNone (default) / Bearer token / API key header
Header nameonly for header; required, 1-128 HTTP token characters, not reserved; placeholder "x-api-key"
API keyonly when auth is not none; type=password, autocomplete=new-password; required on create, optional on edit when hasKey; never echoed back

Behavior

  • Load: GET /api/agents/:id/mcp. Use profiles for "Yours" and tenantProfiles for attached workspace servers. For admins, profiles also contains tenant servers (legacy); split by scope so each server appears once, in its tab.
  • Attach: POST /api/agents/:id/mcp { profileIds } (at most 50 ids, each at most 200 chars) replaces the caller's attachments. Then onSaved() bumps mcpVersion.
  • Create: POST /api/mcp { name, transport: "http", url, auth, apiKey? }. Edit: PATCH /api/mcp/:id with changed fields only; omit apiKey to keep it. Delete: DELETE /api/mcp/:id, then drop it from selected. Tenant equivalents under /api/tenant/mcp/:id for admins.
  • Workspace tab fetches GET /api/tenant/mcp on first open. 403 sets tenantDenied and shows the note; any tenant route 403 for a non-admin is never shown as an error.
  • Live status (BE-06): subscribe to mcp.status events of the active session for LED and tool count. Sign-in opens the OAuth start URL from BE-06 in a popup; on completion the status event flips to connected. Until BE-06, the LED, tool count and sign-in button do not render and the row shows transport and host only.
  • The topbar tool-health button (Shell) reads the same status and opens this sheet.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Each row: checkbox label = server name; badges and warnings linked via aria-describedby.
  • LED has role="img" and aria-label "Connected" / "Connecting" / "Sign-in needed" / "Can't connect" / "Unavailable".
  • Delete confirm moves focus to "Delete"; Escape or "Keep" returns focus to the Delete icon.
  • Notices use role=status; errors role=alert.

Acceptance

  • A tenant server shows "Workspace" and no edit or delete for a non-admin.
  • A user server with shadowed: true is dimmed and shows the shadowed warning.
  • Editing without typing a key sends no apiKey, and hasKey stays true.
  • Deleting lists the attached agents by name.
  • A non-admin opening Workspace sees the note, not a red banner.
  • Without BE-06, no LED or sign-in control renders.
  • The new-chats note is visible in every state except No agent.

  • ConnectedTools (pill summarising attached servers, up to 3 .tool-chip + "+N", states "Loading tools…", "Tools unavailable", "Connect tools"). Out of scope: its job moves to the topbar tool-health button, which shows the worst server state and opens the Connected tools sheet (Shell). Its aria copy "Connected tools: a, b (unavailable). User actions it offered (fork, compact, model, effort, archive) are covered by slash commands and QuickTools (Composer). If kept, it lives only in dev mode behind D-04 in the tools sheet; otherwise delete it.

Acceptance

  • No production route imports either component.

Session panel and insights

The session panel is the right-hand aside that holds the per-session views: Activity, Goal, Agents, Plan, Insights and a new Changes tab. This part also owns the three observability levels that live in the chat: the receipt under each answer (level 1), the trace card (level 2) and the developer details (level 3), plus every chart, meter and formatter they share. v3 keeps today's data and math, puts the plain-language outcome first, turns privacy findings and usage limits into actions, and adds a This turn / Session scope to the panel.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §6 (observability) and §3.15 (SessionActivity). Target design: design/.cv3-parts/obs.html; the Activity and Plan tab designs come from the r2 panel boards (design/.cv2r2-parts/panel.html), which v3 kept. Existing spec values: truex-design-spec.html #s-panel, #s-activity, #s-plan, #s-insights. The Goal tab and goal strip are specified in Goal strip and the Agents tab in Agents. The turn state every status surface reads is deriveTurnState() in Shell.

Token rules for this part: text under 13px uses --ink-2. Chart series use --series-1..3 and --series-other; gridlines --chart-grid; axis text --chart-axis. Semantic states use --warn/--warning-bg/--warning-text, --bad/--bad-bg and --ok/--ok-bg. Motion uses --dur-* and --ease-*. All of these come from Foundations. Raw values quoted below are today's CSS; the named token replaces each at the same value.

Data

export const SESSION_TABS = ["activity","goal","agents","plan","insights","changes"] as const; // v3 order
export type SessionTab = (typeof SESSION_TABS)[number];
export type PanelScope = "turn" | "session";                          // derive

// proposal D-NEW-G1: what the page remembers per viewer (localStorage, try/catch)
interface PanelPrefs {
  open: boolean;                  // was the activity panel open
  tab: SessionTab;                // last manual tab pick
  size: "min" | "max";            // list-mode size
  width?: number;                 // last dragged width, clamped 360..560
  scope: Partial<Record<SessionTab, PanelScope>>;
}
const PANEL_PREFS_KEY = "truex:panel";                                 // proposal D-NEW-G1

Behavior

  • Width fitting stays fitPanel(vw, PANEL_W[size], CHAT_MIN[size], …) (see Shell). A dragged width replaces PANEL_W[size] as input and is still capped by innerWidth − 20.
  • Crossing from >900 to ≤900 closes the panel (exists). At ≤900 it opens only on a user action; Follow never auto-opens the drawer.
  • Persistence proposal D-NEW-G1: write PanelPrefs on every open, close, manual tab pick, size toggle and drag end (debounced 300ms). On load, restore tab, size, width and scope always; restore open only when vw > 900. Storage failures fall back to defaults silently.
  • A manual tab pick calls follow.manual() and holds for MANUAL_HOLD_MS = 8000 (exists). Follow requests within FOLLOW_BATCH_MS = 300 coalesce (exists).
  • Non-Activity tabs remount on switch (keyed by tab), as today.
  • Drawer at ≤900: focus moves into the panel on open and back to the opener on close. Tapping the scrim closes it.

Keyboard and a11y

  • mod+. toggles the panel (global, fires while typing). Esc closes it after menus and goal mode (Esc order in Shell).
  • div.tabs[role=tablist], button.tab[role=tab][aria-selected][aria-controls=session-tabpanel]; ArrowLeft/Right, Home, End move between tabs (exists). Roving tabIndex.
  • .p-resize is role=separator, aria-orientation=vertical, aria-valuemin=360, aria-valuemax=560, aria-valuenow, aria-label "Resize panel", focusable; ArrowLeft/Right change width by 20px, Home/End jump to 560/360.
  • Drawer mode: aria-modal=true and focus trapped while open.

Acceptance

  • Dragging the handle never gives a width outside 360..560, and the chat never drops below CHAT_MIN without the panel becoming an overlay.
  • At 800px the panel opens as a drawer with a scrim; tapping the scrim closes it and focus returns to the opener.
  • Reloading keeps the last tab, size and width; the panel reopens only when vw > 900.
  • With storage blocked the panel still opens, switches tabs and resizes.
  • With reduced motion the width changes without a transition.
  • Changes tab is absent when the changesTab flag is off.

Data

interface TurnRef {             // derive from events: turn.started / turn.completed
  turnId: string;
  index: number;                // 1-based "T{n}"
  startedAt: string;
  prompt: string;               // first user message text of the turn
  kind: "turn" | "steer";       // steer = message sent with steer:true
  status: "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "interrupted"; // from TurnTrace.status (free string today, BE-05 enum)
}
interface PanelScopeState {
  scope: Record<SessionTab, PanelScope>;
  selectedTurnId: string | null; // null = follow live / last
  liveTurnId: string | null;     // running turn
}

Behavior

  • Defaults: Activity and Agents → turn; Goal (locked), Plan, Insights, Changes → session. Choice is remembered per tab (PanelPrefs.scope).
  • Follow: with no manual pick, the selected turn is the live turn while one runs, else the last turn.
  • Clicking a message in the stream selects its turn (needs turnId on messages, which entries already carry as item:{turnId}:{id} keys). Clicking a chip scrolls the stream to the turn's first message.
  • The panel never moves away from a turn the user picked. Back to live clears the pick and scrolls the stream to the bottom.
  • Slicing rule: per-turn data is only events tagged with that turnId; session data is a sum (tokens, time, counts) or a history (plans, file edits).

Keyboard and a11y

  • Segmented is role=radiogroup with aria-label "Scope"; options role=radio, arrow keys move.
  • Rail is role=listbox aria-label "Turns"; chips role=option with aria-label "Turn {n}, {time}, {status}".
  • Selecting a turn announces "Showing turn {n}" in a polite live region.

Acceptance

  • Picking T2 while T4 runs keeps T2 selected as new events arrive; Back to live shows and returns to T4.
  • Plan on Session and Activity on This turn persist independently across reloads.
  • Goal shows This turn disabled with "Goal spans all turns".

Data

type LogKind = "thinking" | "tool" | "command" | "fileChange" | "plan" | "helper" | "error" | "turn";
interface LogRow {                 // derive: DomainEvent[] filtered by turnId
  id: string; turnId: string; kind: LogKind;
  title: string;                   // today's event label rules
  meta?: string;                   // duration via formatDuration, or "Helper agent"
  at: string;                      // time label
  status?: StepSpan["status"];
  progress?: number | null;        // 0..1, BE-04 item progress
  helperThreadId?: string;         // nests under its spawning row
}
interface TurnStats {              // derive
  durationMs: number | null;       // TurnTrace.totalMs, or now − startedAt while running
  tokens: number;                  // turnTokens(trace) or liveUsage main total
  toolCalls: number;               // steps with kind command | tool | webSearch
  files: number;                   // distinct paths in fileChange items
  errors: number;                  // steps failed + error events
}

Behavior

  • Rows are oldest first. Thinking shows "Thought" plus word count, never a duration (hard fact).
  • During a turn, only events already streamed appear. Live tool rows need item.started/item.completed for every item type streamed to the panel (BE-04); until then tool rows appear when the trace lands on turn.completed.
  • Session scope: totals first (turns, tokens main plus helpers, working time = sum of totalMs, not wall clock, files, errors); then groups, newest selected turn open. Clicking a group's chip switches to This turn with that turn selected.
  • Errors stay in their turn's group with their ref (code · requestId) and fix action. The session error count keeps them findable.
  • Session scope ends with a one-line pointer "{n} files changed · Open Changes" when Changes is enabled.

Keyboard and a11y

  • span.live-title[role=status] (exists). Log is ol with aria-label "Work log for turn {n}".
  • Groups are native details/summary; summary aria-label includes the mini stats sentence.

Acceptance

  • Selecting T2 shows only T2 rows; no T1 or T3 helper appears.
  • A turn with no helpers shows the empty-slice row with the session helper count.
  • Session working time equals the sum of totalMs, not end minus start.
  • Thinking rows never show a duration.

Data

// existing
export interface PlanStep { step: string; status: string } // stepStatus() → pending | inProgress | completed
// derive: lib/plan-history.ts
interface PlanVersion {
  version: number;                 // 1-based, client counter
  createdTurnId: string | null;    // turnId of the plan.updated event
  steps: PlanStep[];
  explanation?: string;            // plan.updated data.explanation
  stepHistory: Record<string, { status: string; turnId: string | null }[]>; // key = normalized step title
  supersededTurnId: string | null;
}
interface PlanDiffRow { op: "kept" | "removed" | "added"; step: string }
function pushPlan(h: PlanVersion[], plan: PlanStep[], turnId: string | null): PlanVersion[];
function diffPlans(a: PlanStep[], b: PlanStep[]): PlanDiffRow[];

Behavior

  • New version rule: a plan.updated whose step titles (trimmed, case-folded) differ from the current version's set or order creates a version. A status-only change updates the current version and appends to stepHistory.
  • diffPlans matches by normalized title; output order is kept steps in b order, then removed (a order), then added (b order), as in the r2 board.
  • History lives in page memory keyed by session id and is dropped on session change. snapshot seeds version 1 only.
  • This turn: steps whose status changed in the selected turn get the tint and "done T{n}" chip. Session: turn chip on every step, no tints.
  • Plan approval stays in the request dock (Approve / Revise).

Keyboard and a11y

  • Progress live region announces "{done} of {total} done" (exists). Diff rows carry sr-only "Removed:" / "Added:" prefixes.
  • Version chips are buttons that expand the matching superseded card and move focus to its summary.

Acceptance

  • A reworded plan in T3 creates v2 and keeps v1 as a superseded card, collapsed.
  • Status changes alone never create a version.
  • The diff for the r2 example lists 1 kept, 4 removed, 3 added.

Data

// BE-04: new DomainEvent
// { type: "diff.updated", turnId, data: { files: FileDiff[] } }
interface FileDiff {             // BE-04
  path: string;
  kind: "add" | "update" | "delete";
  added: number; removed: number;
  diff?: string;                 // unified diff for this turn
  itemId: string;                // fileChange item id
}
interface SessionFile {          // derive: fold diff.updated by path
  path: string;
  added: number; removed: number; // net over turns
  edits: { turnId: string; added: number; removed: number; kind: FileDiff["kind"]; diff?: string }[];
  writing: boolean;               // latest edit belongs to the running turn
}

Behavior

  • Order: most recently edited first. This turn scope filters to files with an edit in the selected turn.
  • Diff text renders as text only, never as HTML.
  • The tab-count is files.length.

Keyboard and a11y

  • List aria-label "Files changed in this session"; turn chips are buttons with aria-expanded and aria-label "Show changes to {path} in turn {n}".
  • Diff pre is tabIndex=0 with aria-label "Diff of {path}".

Acceptance

  • Two edits to one file in T1 and T3 show one row with chips T1 (created) and T3 and summed net lines.
  • A file being written in the live turn shows "writing" and its counts grow.

Trace data model

Verbatim from shared/contracts.ts with v3 additions marked. Fields without a marker exist today. threadId is stripped from public responses. There is no cost or currency anywhere today; the only "cost" is token counts.

export type StepKind =
  | "thinking" | "message" | "command" | "tool"
  | "fileChange" | "webSearch" | "agent" | "other";

export interface StepSpan {
  id: string;
  kind: StepKind;
  label: string;                 // plain words, never raw args
  agent: string;                 // "main" or helper nickname/role
  agentThreadId: string;
  startMs: number;               // offset from turn start
  durationMs: number | null;     // null while running
  status: "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "declined";
  error?: StepError;             // BE-05
  words?: number;                // BE-11: thinking word count (else derive from reasoning text)
  thinkingMs?: number;           // BE-11: thinking duration; absent today, never show a thinking duration without it
}
export interface StepError {     // BE-05
  code: string;                  // e.g. "notShared", "authExpired"; UI maps code → fix, never hard-codes names
  message: string;               // plain-language, safe to show
  resource?: { kind: "file" | "folder" | "tool" | "server"; name: string; id?: string };
  ref?: string;                  // "code · requestId"
  retryable?: boolean;           // BE-05 retry step
}
export interface TokenCounts {
  inputTokens: number; cachedInputTokens: number;
  outputTokens: number; reasoningOutputTokens: number; totalTokens: number;
}
export interface TurnUsage extends TokenCounts {
  contextWindow: number | null;
  contextUsedTokens: number | null;
}
export interface RateLimitView {
  limitName: string | null;
  primaryUsedPercent: number | null;
  primaryWindowMins: number | null;
  primaryResetsAt: number | null;    // BE-21: must be sent reliably (unix s or ms)
  secondaryUsedPercent: number | null;
  secondaryWindowMins: number | null;
  secondaryResetsAt: number | null;  // BE-21
  reached: string | null;
  at: string;
}
export type PrivacyKind = "email"|"phone"|"card"|"iban"|"ssn"|"aadhaar"|"pan"|"ip"|"secret";
export type PrivacySource = "userMessage"|"toolOutput"|"command"|"fileContent"|"assistant";
export interface PrivacyFinding {
  kind: PrivacyKind; source: PrivacySource; count: number;
  sample: string;                  // masked; shown only in developer mode (D-04)
  resource?: string;               // BE-20: file or tool name the text came from
  agentThreadId?: string;          // BE-20: helper that read it
  stepId?: string;                 // BE-20: StepSpan.id
}
export interface PrivacyReport { scannedChars: number; findings: PrivacyFinding[] }
export type TurnStatus = "completed" | "failed" | "interrupted"; // BE-05 (free string today)
export interface TurnTrace {
  turnId: string;
  threadId?: string;
  startedAt: string;
  totalMs: number | null;
  status: string;                  // BE-05: narrow to TurnStatus

Privacy vocabulary (shared/privacy.ts)

Exists, unchanged. privacyLabels: email "email address", phone "phone number", card "card number", iban "bank account (IBAN)", ssn "social security number", aadhaar "Aadhaar number", pan "PAN number", ip "IP address", secret "secret or access key". Source labels: userMessage "your message", toolOutput "a tool output", command "a command", fileContent "file content", assistant "the reply". describeFinding(f) gives "2 email addresses in a tool output". scanText(text, source) groups by kind with one masked sample (j***@***.com). MAX_SCAN_CHARS = 200_000. Raw values never reach the browser.

Token math (exists)

  • splitTokens(u): cached = clamp(cachedInputTokens, 0, inputTokens); newInput = inputTokens − cached; reasoning = clamp(reasoningOutputTokens, 0, outputTokens); output = outputTokens − reasoning; total = sum of the four. Null gives zeros.
  • tokenSegments order and labels: newInput "New input", cached "Cached input", output "Reply", reasoning "Reasoning".
  • turnCounts(t) adds usage and helperUsage field by field. turnTokens(t) = turnCounts(t)?.totalTokens ?? 0.
  • contextFraction(u) = contextUsedTokens / contextWindow, clamped 0..1; null when no window or contextUsedTokens === null.

Session summary (exists)

  • summarize(traces): turns = count; avgTotalMs = mean of numeric totalMs; p95TotalMs = percentile(times, .95) nearest rank (sorted[ceil(p·n)−1]); main token fields summed from usage; helperTokens sums helperUsage.totalTokens; privacyFindings sums counts.
  • cachedFraction(s) = cachedInputTokens / inputTokens, null with no input. totalTokens(s) = inputTokens + outputTokens + helperTokens (reasoning is inside output).

Privacy lines (exist)

  • findingCount(f) sums f.count.
  • privacyLine([]) = {tone:"ok", text:"No personal data detected"}. Never say "clean". Else describeFinding(first) + " and N more", N = summed count of the rest.
  • draftNote(findings): de-duplicated by kind, "a"/"an" by leading vowel, three or more joined "a, b and c"; "This looks like a phone number and an email address. It will be sent to the model."; empty gives "".

Receipt, timeline, limits (exist)

  • receipt(t): duration = formatDuration(totalMs) or null; tokens = "{formatTokens(turnTokens)} tokens" or null when 0; privacy = privacyLine; label "Took 4.2s, used 12.3k tokens, No personal data detected".
  • timelineLayout(t, nowMs?): see StepTimeline.
  • windowLabel(mins): null or 0 "Usage limit"; 10080 "Weekly limit", multiples "N-week limit"; 1440 "Daily limit", multiples "N-day limit"; multiples of 60 "N-hour limit"; else "N-minute limit".
  • resetsIn(resetsAt, now): unix seconds below 1e12, else ms; past "resets now"; < 1h "resets in 23m" (minutes rounded up); < 1d "resets in 3h 5m"; else "resets in 2d 4h".
  • limitMeters(r, now): 0 to 2 meters, primary then secondary, only when *UsedPercent !== null, clamped 0..100.

Acceptance

  • formatDuration(4290) is "4.2s"; formatDuration(120000) is "2m"; formatDuration(-5) is "0ms".
  • formatPercent(0.004) is "<1%"; formatPercent(null) is "—".
  • formatTokens(12000) is "12k".
  • resetsIn(now − 1, now) is "resets now"; a value below 1e12 is read as seconds.
  • privacyLine never returns the word "clean".

Data

interface TurnReceiptProps { trace: TurnTrace; sessionId?: string }
// derive: outcomeLine(t)
//  group steps by kind in first-start order; each group → phrase:
//   fileChange/command/tool/webSearch → step.label when one step, else "{verb} {n} {noun}"
//   agent → "asked {n} helper(s)"; message → "wrote the answer"; thinking → omitted
//  join phrases with ", " (wireframe form "A, B, C"); capitalize the first letter;
//  at most 3 phrases, then ", and more" (proposal D-NEW-G7)
interface FixAction { label: string; kind: "openUrl" | "reconnect" | "retryStep" | "share"; target?: string } // mapped from StepError.code

Behavior

  • Renders when traceByTurn.has(turnId) && !active (exists). Order: receipt line, problem line, card.
  • Fix buttons come from a client map of error.code to actions. Unknown codes show no button and the ref in 12px mono. Resource names come from error.resource.name, never hard-coded.
  • A problem line also raises the Needs-you count (see Shell) proposal D-NEW-G6.
  • cardId = "trace-" + turnId, non-word characters replaced with "-" (exists).

Keyboard and a11y

  • Details is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls={cardId} while open. The outcome and meta are inside its accessible name via aria-label.
  • Problem line is role=status when it first appears; fix buttons follow it in tab order.
  • The ghost chip is aria-hidden.

// timelineLayout(t, nowMs?) (exists)
//  spanMs = max(1, totalMs, nowMs, every start + duration)
//  lanes keyed by "main" | agentThreadId || agent; main first, label "Assistant"
//  left  = start / spanMs · 100
//  width = min(100 − left, max(1.5, dur / spanMs · 100))   // min 1.5%
//  running step (durationMs null) extends to span end
//  slowest = completed step with largest duration, only when steps.length > 1
// stepKindLabels fallback: thinking "Thinking", message "Writing the reply", command "Ran a command",

//  agent "Worked with a helper", other "Other step"; final fallback "Step"

Behavior

  • List is sorted by start time. Helper steps add " · {lane label}".
  • Live waterfall (BE-04): a trace card for the running turn exists only when the backend streams step.started/step.ended. It ticks via useClock (1s) while any step runs. On turn.completed the final trace replaces it in place. Without BE-04, no card shows until completion, as today.
  • Colour is used only for meaning: slow, failed, running. Helper tone comes from helper order, never from a name.

Keyboard and a11y

  • The waterfall is aria-hidden; ol.tc-steps[aria-label="Steps in order"] is the text alternative (exists). Bars keep a native title "{label} · {duration}".
  • The scroll wrapper is tabIndex=0 with aria-label "Timing waterfall, scrolls sideways" so keyboard users can scroll it.

Acceptance

  • A 3px step at the end of a long turn is still visible (min-width 1.5%, 3px).
  • Two overlapping helper steps never cover each other.
  • At 400px wide the waterfall scrolls inside its wrapper; the page does not.
  • Thinking never shows a duration unless thinkingMs is present.

Chart rules

deriveP1 applies to StackedBar, ShareBar, Meter, ColumnChart, ContextRing, waterfall, Insights bar lists
  • Colour only for meaning. Series: main agent --series-other; helpers by spawn order --series-1..3; four or more helpers fold into "Other" (--series-other) when a chart shows them as separate series.
  • Semantic colours: --warn for slow and near-limit, --bad for failed and critical, --ok for "no personal data". Never use them as series colours.
  • Gridlines --chart-grid 1px; axis text --chart-axis at 10-11px mono. Never a literal colour in chart CSS or SVG attributes; SVG fills use fill: var(--token) in CSS.
  • Every chart has a text alternative: role=img + aria-label, SVG <title>, or an adjacent list. Legends always show values.
  • Numbers are tabular (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) and use the formatters in lib/observability.ts.
  • Width transitions use --dur-5 --ease-std; reduced motion sets them to 0s through the Foundations override.
  • Charts never set a width over 360px; wide content (waterfall) scrolls inside its own wrapper.

State, data and API

This part is the contract layer under every other part: the fetch client, every endpoint the v3 UI calls, the entity types, the one derived turn state, the event stream and its health states, auth and the read-only viewer, feature flags and where client state lives. Other parts reference this one for data; this part links back to them for component detail instead of redefining it.

Source of truth for today's values: chat-ui-schema.md §7 (and §1 for Home state). Target design for the health and viewer states: the Edge states board (design/.cv3-parts/states.html). In this part page means Home in frontend/app/page.tsx. The browser never sees raw runtime data: every shape below is the projection from platform/src/public.ts.

Fix first (production risk, BE-01). api() calls fetch without credentials: "include", and EventSource is created without withCredentials. With AUTH_MODE=google and the frontend on a different origin from the platform, the session cookie is never sent. Every call then returns 401 and the stream never opens. This blocks sign-in in any cross-origin deploy and must land before any P1 screen. The client half is in api() client, the server half in CORS and cookies.

Client plumbing

api() client

existsBE-01P1 frontend/lib/api.ts · also lib/transport.ts subscribe()

One function performs every JSON call and turns every failure into an ApiRequestError. v3 keeps the call shape and the error model, adds credentials, adds verbs (needed by BE-07 and later items) and adds one global handler for 401 and ownership 403.

Data

// frontend/lib/api.ts
export class ApiRequestError extends Error {
  status: number;      // HTTP status, 0 for network or timeout
  code: string;        // server code, or HTTP_<status>, NETWORK_ERROR, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, INVALID_RESPONSE
  requestId?: string;  // body.requestId or x-request-id header
}
export interface ErrorRef { code?: string; requestId?: string; turnId?: string }
interface ServerErrorBody { error: string; code: string; requestId: string } // errorHandler

type ApiInit = {                       // derive (v3)
  method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  body?: unknown;
  timeoutMs?: number;                  // default 45000
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  quiet?: boolean;                     // skip onAuthError (background polls)
};
export function api<T>(path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T>;   // exists
export function api<T>(path: string, init: ApiInit): Promise<T>;    // derive

// One listener, set by Home. Called after the error is built, before it is thrown.
export function setAuthErrorHandler(fn: (e: ApiRequestError, path: string) => void): void; // derive
export function userMessage(err: unknown, fallback: string): string;   // exists
export function errorRef(err: unknown): ErrorRef | null;               // exists
export function warnFailure(tag: string, err: unknown): void;          // exists, quiet

Behavior

  • Overload detection: the second argument is an ApiInit only when it is a plain object with a method key. Existing callers that POST a body object without method keep working.
  • Message shown to the user: body.error verbatim when present, else the fallback below by status. Never show code as the headline; it goes in the ref line (ErrorRef).
  • onAuthError routing: status 401 opens the sign-in sheet. Status 403 with NOT_SESSION_OWNER or NOT_PROJECT_OWNER shows the permission toast and flips the view to read-only. 403 CAPABILITY_DENIED shows the toast only. 403 TENANT_DISABLED and NOT_A_MEMBER open the sign-in sheet in its workspace variant. All other errors go only to the caller. derive
  • Callers that pass quiet: true (sidebar refresh, timings, traces, features) never trigger the sheet; they use warnFailure. The next foreground call will.
  • A 502/503/504 on POST /messages may have been accepted. The composer keeps the clientId and a retry replays it; the server answers { duplicate: true } instead of a second turn (exists).
  • /api/features failure is treated as flags off (exists). GET /api/sessions/:id never fails on runtime outage; it returns snapshot: null and recoveryError (exists).

Status fallbacks (exists)

StatusFallback copyGlobal reaction (v3)
0 networkcaller fallbacknone; stream health handles connectivity
400The request is invalid. Check your input.none
401Your session is not authenticated. Sign in again.sign-in sheet
403You do not have permission to perform this operation.toast; owner codes also flip to read-only
404The requested conversation, agent, or file was not found.on the open session: "This conversation is no longer available" empty state, see Shell errors
409The request conflicts with the conversation's current state. Refresh it before retrying.request cards hide stale cards (Requests)
410server message (THREAD_LOST)set session.status = "dead" locally, show the dead banner
413The request is too large. Reduce the attachment or message size.none
422The request could not be processed. Check your input and agent configuration.none
429Too many requests. Wait before trying again.none (only /auth is limited, 60/min)
502 / 503 / 504Invalid response / temporarily unavailable / timed out (may have been accepted)none

Server error codes the UI can meet (exists)

INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_JSON, REQUEST_TOO_LARGE, CONFLICT, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, PLATFORM_INTERNAL, UNAUTHENTICATED (401), WRONG_APP (403), CSRF_ORIGIN (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), CAPABILITY_DENIED (403), SESSION_NOT_FOUND / PROJECT_NOT_FOUND (404), NOT_SESSION_OWNER / NOT_PROJECT_OWNER (403), THREAD_LOST (410), OWNER_UNAVAILABLE / OWNER_UNCONFIGURED / STREAM_UNAVAILABLE (503/502), DUPLICATE_MESSAGE (409), FEATURE_DISABLED (404), INVALID_APPROVAL_MODE (422), INVALID_REVIEW (400), GOAL_NOT_COMPLETE (409), MODEL_UNAVAILABLE (422), AGENT_HANDLE_TAKEN (409), INVALID_PROJECT, TENANT_DISABLED (403), NOT_A_MEMBER (403). Code strings are read from the error, never hard-coded into copy.

Acceptance

  • Every request in the network panel carries the session cookie when frontend and platform are on different origins.
  • The EventSource request carries the cookie and opens in google mode cross-origin.
  • api("/api/agents/x", { method: "DELETE" }) sends DELETE; api("/api/projects", { name }) still sends POST.
  • A 401 from any foreground call opens the sign-in sheet once, even if three calls fail together.
  • A 401 from a quiet poll does not open the sheet.
  • A timed-out send shows "timed out (may have been accepted)" and a retry does not create a second turn.

CORS and cookies (server half of BE-01)

BE-01P1 platform/src/http.ts middleware · platform/src/auth.ts cookie

What the platform must return so credentialed calls from the browser work. This is a backend task; it is listed here because the UI cannot be tested cross-origin without it.

Rules

ItemRequired value
Access-Control-Allow-Originthe exact request Origin when it is in the allowed list (the same list the CSRF check uses). Never *, which browsers reject with credentials
Access-Control-Allow-Credentialstrue
VaryOrigin
Preflight OPTIONS204; Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE; Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Last-Event-ID; Max-Age: 600
Access-Control-Expose-Headersx-request-id, so ApiRequestError.requestId is readable
SSE routesame CORS headers on GET /api/sessions/:id/events
CookieHTTP-only (exists). Same-site deploy (for example app. and api. on one domain): SameSite=Lax; Secure. Cross-site deploy: SameSite=None; Secure
CSRFunchanged: state-changing /api and /auth requests need an allowed Origin and JSON, else 403 CSRF_ORIGIN
Allowed-origin list configuration name and the same-site vs cross-site deploy choice are open: D-NEW-D1. Default: same-site with SameSite=Lax, which keeps the CSRF surface smallest.

Acceptance

  • A request from an unlisted origin gets no Allow-Origin header and the browser blocks it.
  • A DELETE from the app origin passes preflight.
  • x-request-id is readable in the browser from a failed call.
