Session, SessionHistory and Snapshot

existsBE-09 BE-10 BE-16P1 shared/contracts.ts · platform/src/public.ts publicSession, publicSnapshot

The conversation as the list, the open chat and the stream see it. PublicSession is the only session shape the UI may read; threadId, agentCoreHost, cwd and approvals never leave the server.

Data

type SessionStatus = "active" | "orphaned" | "dead";
// active: normal. orphaned: runtime host unreachable, resumes on next message.
// dead: thread lost, every runtime call returns 410 THREAD_LOST, history read-only.

interface PublicSession {
  _id: string;                       // "sess_" + uuid
  userId?: string;                   // owner; only when set
  agentId: string;
  title?: string;                    // list fills untitled with first user message, 80 chars
  status: SessionStatus;
  createdAt: string;                 // ISO
  goal?: { objective: string; status: GoalStatus };   // trimmed
  projectId?: string;                // only when set
  approvalMode?: ApprovalMode;       // only when the approval-modes flag is on
  // v3 additions
  archived?: boolean;                // BE-16 (list with ?archived=1; today stored, not projected)
  turnState?: "idle" | "running" | "waiting" | "failed";  // BE-16, list rows only
  pendingCount?: number;             // BE-16, list rows only
  ownerName?: string;                // BE-09, display name of userId
  delegation?: { mode: "explicitRequestOnly" | "proactive"; maxConcurrent: number }; // BE-10
  settings?: { model?: string; effort?: string };     // BE-NEW: session settings
}

interface SessionHistory {           // GET /api/sessions/:id
  session: PublicSession;
  messages: Message[];               // ordered transcript
  snapshot: PublicSnapshot | null;   // null when runtime unreachable
  plan: { steps: PlanStep[]; explanation?: string; turnId?: string; updatedAt?: string } | null;
  approvals: ApprovalRecord[];       // resolved-request audit trail
  goalReview: GoalReview | null;
  goalHistory: GoalHistoryEntry[];
  recoveryError: string | null;      // "Conversation recovery: ..."
  recoveryErrorRef: { code: string; requestId?: string } | null;
  viewer?: ViewerAccess;             // BE-09, see Auth
}

interface PublicSnapshot {           // first frame of every connection
  cursor: string;
  state: { kind: "idle" | "starting" | "running" | "interrupting"; turnId?: string };
  messages: { id: string; turnId?: string; text: string; final: boolean; messageIndex?: number }[];
  pending: PendingRequest[];
  plan: PlanStep[];                  // falls back to the saved plan
  goal: Goal | null;
  diff: "";                          // always empty publicly (BE-04 to populate)
  timings: TurnTiming[];
  traces: TurnTrace[];               // recent completed turns, oldest first
  rateLimits: RateLimitView | null;
  subAgents: SubAgent[];
  thinking: { id: string; turnId?: string; summary: string; raw: string; done: boolean }[];
}

Behavior

  • Owner check: isOwner = !session.userId || session.userId === me.user.id. A session with no userId (dev mode, legacy) is treated as owned. Until /api/me resolves, treat as owned and let a 403 flip it (the server is the guard).
  • snapshot === null with recoveryError: render history from messages, show the orphaned banner, keep the composer (the next send resumes).
  • archived is read from the list row when present; after thread/archive succeeds set it locally.

Turn, usage and trace types

existsBE-05 BE-11 BE-20 BE-21P1 shared/contracts.ts · platform/src/public.ts publicTrace

There is no Turn entity. A turn is a turnId that appears on messages, events, timings, traces and requests.

Data

type RuntimeTurnKind = "idle" | "starting" | "running" | "interrupting"; // snapshot.state.kind
type TurnEndStatus = "completed" | "failed" | "interrupted";

interface TurnTiming {
  turnId: string; acceptMs: number | null; ttftMs: number | null;
  streamMs: number; adapterStreamMs: number; idleStreamMs: number; maxGapMs: number;
  deltaRate: number; finalizeMs: number; totalMs: number; deltaCount: number;
  nonStreaming: boolean; status: string;   // projected to TurnEndStatus
}
interface TurnTrace {
  turnId: string; startedAt: string; totalMs: number | null;
  status: string;                  // today free string; BE-05 narrows to TurnEndStatus | "completedWithErrors"
  model?: string;
  steps: StepSpan[];               // max 300
  usage: TurnUsage | null; helperUsage: TokenCounts | null;
  rateLimits: RateLimitView | null; privacy: PrivacyReport;
  costUsd?: number;                // BE-11
  currency?: string;               // BE-11, ISO 4217
}
type StepKind = "thinking" | "message" | "command" | "tool" | "fileChange" | "webSearch" | "agent" | "other";
interface StepSpan {
  id: string; kind: StepKind;
  label: string;                   // plain words, ≤120 chars, never raw args
  agent: string; agentThreadId: string;   // "main" for the main agent
  startMs: number; durationMs: number | null;
  status: "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "declined";
  error?: { message: string; code?: string };   // BE-05
}
interface TurnContext { turnId: string; reconstructed: true;
  sections: { kind: "user" | "toolOutput" | "command" | "fileContent" | "assistant";
              label: string; text: string; chars: number }[];
  truncated: boolean }
interface TraceSummary { turns: number; avgTotalMs: number | null; p95TotalMs: number | null;
  inputTokens: number; cachedInputTokens: number; outputTokens: number;
  reasoningOutputTokens: number; helperTokens: number; privacyFindings: number }
interface SessionTraces { traces: TurnTrace[]; summary: TraceSummary }

interface TokenCounts { inputTokens: number; cachedInputTokens: number; outputTokens: number;
  reasoningOutputTokens: number; totalTokens: number }
interface TurnUsage extends TokenCounts {
  contextWindow: number | null;
  contextUsedTokens: number | null;    // context fullness
}
interface RateLimitView {
  limitName: string | null;
  primaryUsedPercent: number | null; primaryWindowMins: number | null; primaryResetsAt: number | null; // epoch s
  secondaryUsedPercent: number | null; secondaryWindowMins: number | null; secondaryResetsAt: number | null;
  reached: string | null; at: string;
}
type PrivacyKind = "email" | "phone" | "card" | "iban" | "ssn" | "aadhaar" | "pan" | "ip" | "secret";
type PrivacySource = "userMessage" | "toolOutput" | "command" | "fileContent" | "assistant";
interface PrivacyFinding {
  kind: PrivacyKind; source: PrivacySource; count: number;
  sample: string;                      // masked, ≤24 chars, dev mode only (D-04)
  resource?: string; agent?: string; stepId?: string;   // BE-20
}
interface PrivacyReport { scannedChars: number; findings: PrivacyFinding[] }

type ErrorReason = "rateLimited" | "quota" | "credentials" | "providerDown" | "contextWindow" | "other";
interface StreamErrorData {            // "error" event data
  message: string; code: string; reason: ErrorReason;
  httpStatus?: number; willRetry?: boolean; turnId?: string;
  resetsAt?: string;                   // BE-21, rateLimited only
}

Behavior

  • A turn's failure placement uses the event turnId, else ErrorRef.turnId, else the latest turn (BE-NEW-S2 makes the first always present).
  • Usage shown to the user is contextUsedTokens / contextWindow; hide the meter when either is null.
  • Rate-limit reset: primaryResetsAt is epoch seconds; convert with * 1000.

The one derived turn state

deriveTurnState (full version)

deriveP1 lib/turn-state.ts · supersedes the 8-state sketch in the Shell part's Topbar block

One pure function turns page state into one turn state. Every surface that shows "is the assistant doing something" reads it: the topbar pill, the helper chip, the dock badge, the Needs-you count freeze, the sidebar row dot, the composer Send/Stop/Steer and the polite live region.

Relation to the Shell part. Shell: Turn state table defines 8 pill states. This block is the full derivation and supersedes that sketch. It adds two finer states that the pill folds back into the Shell ones: sending shows as Starting, and interrupting shows as Stopping. So the pill labels, tones and priority in the Shell part stay valid. TurnView's pill field is the Shell's TurnState, and the Shell's field names are kept.

States

StateMeaningInputs (after higher rows fail)Pill (Shell)ComposerTag
reconnectingstream is not livestream.phase is reconnecting, disconnected or resyncingreconnecting: "Reconnecting…", "Still reconnecting…" after 30s, "Disconnected", "Refreshing…"Send allowed (POST works without the stream); Stop kept if runningexists
failedlast turn ended in error, no retry pendingfailure && !retryingfailed "Failed"Sendexists
interruptingserver accepted the stop, turn still closingrunning && (stop.phase === "acked" || runtime.kind === "interrupting")stopping "Stopping"Stop disabled, Steer hidden, Send queuesderive
stoppingStop pressed, interrupt POST in flightrunning && stop.phase === "requested"stopping "Stopping"Stop shows spinner, disabledderive
waitingturn blocked on a personrunning && pending.length > 0waiting "Waiting on you" (viewer: "Waiting on {ownerName}")Send queues; Steer allowedderive
workingturn streamingrunning (label: retrying › goal active › plain)working "Working" · "Working on goal" · "Retrying…"Stop, Steer, Send queuesexists
startingmessage accepted, no turn.started yetsend.phase === "accepted" or runtime.kind === "starting"starting "Starting"Stop enabled (interrupt works after accept)derive
sendingPOST in flight, no turnId yetbusy && send.phase === "posting"starting "Starting"textarea and Send disabled; no Stopderive
interruptedlast turn was stoppedlastTurnEnd === "interrupted"interrupted "Stopped"Sendexists
idlenothing happeningotherwiseidle "Ready"Sendexists

Priority (first match wins): reconnecting › failed › interrupting › stopping › waiting › working › starting › sending › interrupted › idle. Folding interrupting into stopping and sending into starting gives exactly the Shell order.

Data

// lib/turn-state.ts
export type TurnStateFull =
  | "idle" | "sending" | "starting" | "working" | "waiting"
  | "stopping" | "interrupting" | "interrupted" | "failed" | "reconnecting";
export type TurnState =                       // the Shell pill state, unchanged
  | "idle" | "starting" | "working" | "waiting"
  | "stopping" | "interrupted" | "failed" | "reconnecting";

export interface TurnInputs {
  running: boolean;                           // exists: turn.started seen, turn.completed not yet
  busy: boolean;                              // exists: a request is in flight
  status: StreamStatus;                       // exists: "Connected" | "Reconnecting" | "Disconnected" | "Mock" | "Not connected"
  stream: StreamHealth;                       // derive: see connection state machine
  slowReconnect: boolean;                     // exists: 30s in reconnecting
  retrying: boolean;                          // exists: error with willRetry: true, no turn.completed yet
  pending: PendingRequest[];                  // exists
  goal: Goal | null;                          // exists
  failure: TurnFailure | null;                // exists
  runtime: { kind: RuntimeTurnKind; turnId?: string } | null;  // snapshot.state, updated by events
  send: { phase: "idle" | "posting" | "accepted"; clientId?: string; turnId?: string }; // derive
  stop: { phase: "idle" | "requested" | "acked"; at?: number };                         // derive
  lastTurnEnd: TurnEndStatus | null;          // derive: from the last turn.completed
  isOwner: boolean;                           // derive: see Auth
  ownerName?: string;                         // BE-09
}

export interface TurnView {
  full: TurnStateFull;
  state: TurnState;                           // Shell name; pill, sidebar dot and dock read this
  label: string;
  indicator: "dot" | "spinner";
  tone: "idle" | "accent" | "warn" | "bad";
  pulse: boolean;                             // false under prefers-reduced-motion
  frozen: boolean;                            // reconnecting: counts hold their last value
  canStop: boolean; canSteer: boolean; sendQueues: boolean;
}

const PILL: Record<TurnStateFull, TurnState> = {
  idle: "idle", sending: "starting", starting: "starting", working: "working",
  waiting: "waiting", stopping: "stopping", interrupting: "stopping",
  interrupted: "interrupted", failed: "failed", reconnecting: "reconnecting",
};

export function deriveFull(i: TurnInputs): TurnStateFull {
  // "idle" (no session) and "connecting" (first open) are not trouble
  if (i.stream.phase === "reconnecting" || i.stream.phase === "disconnected"
      || i.stream.phase === "resyncing") return "reconnecting";
  if (i.failure && !i.retrying) return "failed";
  if (i.running && (i.stop.phase === "acked" || i.runtime?.kind === "interrupting")) return "interrupting";
  if (i.running && i.stop.phase === "requested") return "stopping";
  if (i.running && i.pending.length > 0) return "waiting";
  if (i.running) return "working";
  if (i.send.phase === "accepted" || i.runtime?.kind === "starting") return "starting";
  if (i.busy && i.send.phase === "posting") return "sending";
  if (i.lastTurnEnd === "interrupted") return "interrupted";
  return "idle";
}

export function deriveTurnState(i: TurnInputs): TurnView {
  const full = deriveFull(i);
  return view(full, PILL[full], i);           // label, tone, indicator from the Shell table
}

function reconnectLabel(i: TurnInputs): string {
  switch (i.stream.phase) {
    case "disconnected": return "Disconnected";
    case "resyncing":    return "Refreshing…";
    default:             return i.slowReconnect ? "Still reconnecting…" : "Reconnecting…";
  }
}

Transitions (who sets each input)

EventSets
Send pressed (not queued)busy = true, send = { phase: "posting", clientId }, failure = null, lastTurnEnd = null
POST /messages 202, steer: falsesend = { phase: "accepted", turnId }, busy = false
POST 202, steer: trueno turn change; send.phase = "idle"; the message joins the running turn
POST failssend.phase = "idle", busy = false; the message row shows delivery: "failed"
turn.startedrunning = true, runtime = { kind: "running", turnId }, send.phase = "idle", failure = null, stop.phase = "idle"
Stop pressedstop = { phase: "requested", at: now }
POST /interrupt okstop.phase = "acked"
POST /interrupt failsstop.phase = "idle"; inline error under Stop "Couldn't stop. Try again."
error with willRetry: trueretrying = true
error with willRetry false or missingretrying = false, failure = { reason, message, httpStatus }
turn.completedrunning = false, runtime.kind = "idle", retrying = false, stop.phase = "idle", lastTurnEnd = turn.status; failed also sets failure from turn.error
snapshotruntime = state; running = kind === "running" || kind === "interrupting"; pending = snapshot.pending; stop.phase = kind === "interrupting" ? "acked" : "idle"

Behavior

  • Stop watchdog: if stop.phase is not idle 15000ms after stop.at and no turn.completed arrived, reload history (GET /api/sessions/:id) and hydrate from its snapshot. proposal D-NEW-D3
  • Starting watchdog: if send.phase === "accepted" for 30000ms with no turn.started and the stream is connected, reload history once. proposal D-NEW-D3
  • Reconnecting wins over everything because every other input may be stale while the stream is down. Counts (frozen) hold their last value.
  • Viewer: the same function runs for viewers; canStop, canSteer and Send are false when !isOwner, and the waiting label uses ownerName (fallback "the owner").
  • Pure: no timers, no Date.now() inside. Timers live in the hook useTurnState() that feeds it.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Live region text is written by the Shell (Topbar) on state change, not full change, so sending → starting → working says "Working" once.

Acceptance

  • A unit test exists for every row, and for these overlaps: reconnecting with pending, failed with running, interrupting with pending, stopping with pending, starting with lastTurnEnd interrupted.
  • PILL[deriveFull(i)] equals the Shell deriveTurnState result for every input the Shell table defines.
  • Between Send and the 202, Stop is not shown; between the 202 and turn.started, Stop is shown and works.
  • A reload during an interrupt shows Stopping (from snapshot.state.kind === "interrupting"), not Working.
  • A steer send never changes the pill.

Streaming protocol

Server-Sent Events through the browser EventSource at GET /api/sessions/:id/events[?cursor=<cursor>]. The platform proxies agent-core's thread SSE, passes Last-Event-ID (or cursor) upstream and filters every frame through publicEvent().

Frame
id: <cursor>\ndata: <JSON DomainEvent>\n\n
Heartbeat
SSE comment : heartbeat; the browser ignores it
Fatal end
named event: stream.error with { code: "STREAM_FAILED" | "STREAM_ENDED", error, requestId? }, then close
Limits
unknown or malformed frames dropped server-side; a frame over 4 MB kills the stream
Ordering
monotonic seq, opaque cursor. A fresh connection starts with snapshot, then deltas
Resume
last lastEventId saved in sessionStorage["cursor:<sessionId>"], sent as ?cursor= on the next subscribe; the browser's own retry sends Last-Event-ID
interface DomainEvent {
  type: DomainType; seq: number; cursor: string; at: string;  // ISO
  threadId: string;   // not copied by publicEvent(): absent in the browser
  turnId?: string; itemId?: string;
  data: Record<string, any>;
}

Typical order: turn.started → (reasoning.delta* / reasoning items / activity.updated* / plan.updated / approval.requested → approval.resolved / subagent.*)* → message.delta* → message.final → usage.updated / limits.updated → turn.completed. A steer send joins the running turn and emits no new turn.started. The mock transport (lib/mock.ts) plays turn.started, reasoning.delta, approval.requested (15s expiry), approval.resolved, word-by-word message.delta (100ms), message.final, usage.updated, turn.completed, and reports status "Mock".

  • Reducer rule: events are applied in seq order. An event with seq at or below the last applied one is ignored (duplicate after reconnect). derive
  • An unparseable frame calls handlers.onResync() without advancing the cursor (exists); treat it exactly like resync.required.
  • The streaming answer is never in a live region. It carries aria-busy="true" while deltas arrive.

Connection state machine

deriveP1 lib/transport.ts subscribe() · new lib/use-stream-health.ts

Today the stream exposes one string, status. v3 wraps it in a small machine so the pill, banners and skeleton read one value with a reason and a ref. status stays for compatibility and is derived from phase.

Data

type StreamStatus = "Connected" | "Reconnecting" | "Disconnected" | "Mock" | "Not connected"; // exists
type StreamPhase =
  | "idle"          // no session open (draft)
  | "connecting"    // first subscribe, before onopen
  | "connected"     // onopen, snapshot received or pending
  | "reconnecting"  // onerror while EventSource retries, or error willRetry at transport level
  | "resyncing"     // resync.required or unparseable frame; reloading history
  | "disconnected"; // CLOSED, or after stream.error
interface StreamHealth {
  phase: StreamPhase;
  since: number;                              // ms epoch of the last phase change
  code?: "STREAM_FAILED" | "STREAM_ENDED" | string;   // from stream.error
  message?: string;                           // server error text, verbatim
  requestId?: string;
  attempts: number;                           // reconnect attempts in this outage
  hydrated: boolean;                          // a snapshot arrived on the current connection
}

Transitions

FromTriggerToSide effects

connectedsnapshot eventconnectedhydrated = true; apply snapshot

reconnecting30000ms elapsedreconnectingslowReconnect = true; show the slow reconnect banner
any openonerror, readyState === CLOSEDdisconnectedstatus = "Disconnected", no code
any openstream.errordisconnectedstore code, message, requestId; close the EventSource

idle ─subscribe→ connecting ─onopen→ connected ─snapshot→ connected(hydrated)
connected ─onerror(CONNECTING)→ reconnecting ─onopen→ connected
                                reconnecting ─30s→ reconnecting(slow)

any ─stream.error | CLOSED→ disconnected ─Reconnect→ connecting

Behavior

  • Auto-reconnect from disconnected: on window.online and on visibilitychange to visible, at most once per 10000ms. STREAM_ENDED also retries once after 3000ms (copy says "Reconnect in a moment"). STREAM_FAILED never auto-retries. proposal D-NEW-D4
  • The EventSource's own retry interval is the browser default; the client does not set retry:.
  • Snapshot hydration keeps rendered entries: messages are merged by id, and entries after the last snapshot message are kept only if they are final. Pending, plan, goal, helpers and rate limits are replaced whole.
  • willRetry on an error event is a provider retry, not a transport state; it does not change phase. It sets retrying (see derivation).
  • POST calls do not wait on the stream. Send while reconnecting still posts; the answer arrives when the stream is back.

Acceptance

  • Killing the platform for 5s shows Reconnecting and then recovers with no duplicate messages.
  • After 30s of reconnecting the pill reads "Still reconnecting…".
  • A stream.error STREAM_FAILED shows the disconnected banner with the server text and does not reconnect on its own.
  • A resync.required keeps every rendered turn on screen and shimmers only the tail.
  • An event with a lower seq than the last applied one changes nothing.

Streaming health UI

The rule from the Edge states board: the pill carries transient trouble, and banners are only for states that need you. Each banner has exactly one recovery action. All banners share one frame, HealthBanner, placed at the top of the chat column under the topbar, above the first message, sticky at --z-sticky. Only one banner shows at a time; priority is sign-in sheet (modal) › disconnected › dead › orphaned › slow reconnect › archived. The 403 toast and the interrupting state are not banners.

Auth and permissions

Auth modes
AUTH_MODE=dev: fixed user dev-user, role default admin; optional x-truex-user / x-truex-role headers when DEV_USER_HEADER=on. AUTH_MODE=google: HTTP-only session cookie with idle and absolute expiry; tenant switch rotates the cookie
CSRF
state-changing /api and /auth requests need an allowed Origin and JSON, else 403 CSRF_ORIGIN
Agents
any user may create agents (alpha, no role check). Tenant MCP management is admin only
Hidden vs denied
hidden records are 404, never 403. A 404 on a session link means "not found or not shared with you"

Data

// derive in Home
const isOwner = !session?.userId || !me || session.userId === me.user.id;
const readOnly = !isOwner || forcedReadOnly;   // forcedReadOnly: set by a 403 NOT_SESSION_OWNER

interface ViewerAccess {                        // BE-09, on SessionHistory
  isOwner: boolean;                             // server truth; wins over the client check
  ownerName?: string;
  canRequestAccess: boolean;
  canDuplicate: boolean;
  trace: "full" | "stepsOnly" | "hidden";       // trace visibility rule
}
// POST /api/sessions/:id/duplicate        → 201 PublicSession (owned by caller)   // BE-09
// POST /api/sessions/:id/access-requests  → 202 { ok: true }                      // BE-09

Behavior

  • readOnly is passed as one prop to every write surface (composer, request dock, goal strip, message actions, helper rows, session menu). Components do not recompute it.
  • Admins see the same read-only view (§7.4 gives admins read only). An admin interrupt is open: D-NEW-D7.
  • Duplicate copies transcript and file refs, no pending requests and no goal, so the copy starts idle and owned by the viewer (wireframe recommendation; D-NEW-D8).
  • The sidebar shows other members' chats only under visibility "all"; they carry no special marker in P2.
  • No write request is ever sent from the viewer UI. The 403 path (toast) is only a guard.

Keyboard and a11y

  • Focus order: skip link goes to the viewer bar instead of the composer ("Skip to actions"). The banner is role="status". No disabled controls exist, so nothing is announced as unavailable.

Acceptance

  • As a viewer, the page has no textarea, no Stop, no request buttons and no Retry, Edit or Regenerate in the DOM.
  • Copy and file downloads work for a viewer.
  • Duplicate opens a new chat owned by the viewer, idle, with the same messages.
  • A chat with no userId is treated as owned.

Accessibility, QA and build plan

This part holds the rules that apply to the whole page. It covers the accessibility spec, the responsive QA matrix, the build plan by phase, every backend item, the decisions register, conflicts between parts, the global acceptance checklist, the definition of done and performance budgets. Component parts own their own keys, labels and states. This part joins them up and settles clashes. Where a part and this part disagree on a cross-part rule, this part wins and the clash is listed under Conflict check.

Inputs: the accessibility and responsive boards in design/.cv3-parts/states.html, the build order board in design/.cv3-parts/system.html, design/convo-v3-plan.html, the global gaps in chat-ui-schema.md (lines 18-51) and the finished parts: Foundations, Shell, Composer, Stream, Requests and Agents. The Panel and Data parts were still being written when this part was drafted, so their component ids are not listed here. Link to those parts by section until their ids exist.

Full WCAG validation needs manual testing with assistive technology (VoiceOver on macOS and iOS, NVDA or JAWS on Windows, TalkBack on Android) and an expert accessibility review. The rules and contrast ratios here are a build target. The ratios were calculated from token hex values, not measured on devices. Meeting this spec does not make the page WCAG compliant.

1. Accessibility spec

This section is the page-wide contract. Foundations owns the focus ring, .sr-only and the contrast table (Focus and accessibility styles, Contrast table). This section says where each rule applies.

Status live region

There is one polite region, owned by the Shell (Topbar). Every part writes to it through one helper, announce(text, { key }). No part adds its own polite region, with two exceptions that already exist: the search palette result count and the in-thread search count. Errors that need action use role=alert on the element that shows them.

  • The streaming answer is never in a live region. The message list carries aria-busy="true" while tokens arrive and aria-busy="false" once turn.completed or turn.failed arrives. Screen-reader users read the answer on demand.
  • Throttle: one message per 1000ms (Shell). A newer message in the window replaces the queued one. Same text within 5000ms is dropped. proposal D-NEW-SH-07
  • Precedence inside one window: a specific request message beats the generic state message. When a request docks, "Waiting on you" is not also said.
  • Text comes from derived state (deriveTurnState()), never from a component's own copy of it.

Esc order

One handler owns Esc, useEscStack. Each open layer pushes an entry, and Esc runs only the top entry, then calls preventDefault and stopPropagation. This replaces the per-part rules, which say the same thing in different words. proposal D-NEW-SH-01

  1. A menu or combobox list (slash, mention, row menu, goal menu, effort list).
  2. A popover (agent, model, dock popover, Share, tray).
  3. The Other input in a question card, when open and empty.
  4. In-thread search.
  5. A modal (sheet, dialog, palette, drawer). A card inside the batch sheet runs D-06 first, and the next Esc closes the sheet.
  6. Focus context:
    • in a docked request card: D-06 (Cancel option, or focus the composer)
    • in the textarea while editing a queued item: cancel the edit
    • in goal mode: leave goal mode, keep the draft
    • in helper detail: back to the list
  7. With focus in the composer and a turn running: stop the turn.

Esc never stops a turn when focus is outside the composer, and never declines a request when focus is in the textarea.

Target sizes

  • Pointer: every interactive target is at least 24×24px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), or has 24px of clear spacing around a smaller target.
  • Touch (@media (pointer: coarse)): the hit area is at least 44×44px. Where the visual stays smaller (26px icon buttons, 20px pills, 18px avatars), a ::after pseudo-element with inset: -9px (or as needed to reach 44px) extends the hit area. Hit areas of neighbours must not overlap, so rows of icon buttons get 4px more gap on coarse pointers. proposal D-NEW-SH-06
  • Known small targets to check: composer ghost cancel 26×26, MCP row icons 26×26, "Sign in" 26px tall, tint circles 26, delegation pill 20, scope badges 18, code block Copy and Wrap, message action buttons, HelperGroup "Open".
  • Inline links in running text are exempt from 2.5.8, but links in rows (citations, file cards) are not.

Screen-reader labels for icon-only buttons

Every icon-only button has an aria-label. The icon is aria-hidden="true". A tooltip, when present, repeats the label and never replaces it. Labels with a variable use the data field, never a hard-coded name. Rows tagged proposal are labels no part has fixed yet. They use the default below until the owner confirms (D-NEW-SH-08).

Contrast

Ratios come from the Foundations contrast table and the States board. They were calculated from token hex values and not measured on devices.

PairRatioRule
--ink-3 #67757C on white4.8:1Pass for text at 13px and up. Text under 13px uses --ink-2
--ink-2 #5F6D73 on white5.4:1Pass
White on --accent-fg #2A72A35.2:1Pass. Every filled button with light text uses this fill
White on --accent #3691CD3.4:1 (3.45:1 in Foundations)Fails for text. --accent is kept for icons, rings and bars only
Dark --ink-3 #8B999F on #1717176.1:1Pass
Dark --on-accent #111213 on dark --accent-fg #BCDEE813.17:1Pass (Foundations D-NEW: dark on-accent)
--border-control against the page1.34:1 light, 1.73:1 darkBelow 3:1 for non-text UI. Kept in v3 because inputs keep a visible label and the focus halo (Foundations D-NEW: input border contrast). Recheck in the high-fidelity pass
  • Status must never be carried by color alone. Every tone (LED, chip, dot) pairs with text or an icon. Where text hides at narrow widths, the accessible name keeps it (see HelperGroup D-NEW-AG-10).
  • Focus ring: 2px --accent outline, 2px offset, radius 8px (Focus styles). It must reach 3:1 against both the element and the page in both themes.
  • Forced colors (@media (forced-colors: active)): focus rings use outline-color: Highlight, and chips and pills keep a 1px border. proposal D-NEW-SH-09

2. Responsive QA matrix

Test each width in both themes with the sidebar open and closed, and the activity panel closed, at min and at max. Breakpoint values come from Foundations breakpoints and Shell breakpoints. At every width: no horizontal page scroll, the composer bar stays on screen, and a docked request plus the composer stay fully visible.

WidthLayout expectedVerify
1440Sidebar docked 268, panel docked at min or max, floating dock, full breadcrumb with project
  • Turn outline rail shows at 4 or more turns (D-NEW-S10)
  • Message column max width holds, and the composer is 740px max
  • Panel max floats only below 1230 with the sidebar closed, so it stays docked here
  • Hover-only actions show on hover and on focus
  • Tooltips on the dock and chips
1180Sidebar docked; the panel yields when it is max (fitPanel rule 4)
  • The outline rail threshold (≥1180) is exactly met, and the rail shows
  • At 1179 it hides with no layout jump in the message column
  • Opening the panel at max with the sidebar open closes or floats as specified
1100bp-xl: the project crumb hides; fitPanel closes the sidebar when the panel opens; composer chips show icons only
  • The stage stays at 460px or wider with the panel open
  • Chip labels hide, and each chip keeps its accessible name and a tooltip
  • Closing the panel does not reopen the sidebar on its own
900bp-lg: the activity panel becomes a fixed overlay drawer (z --z-drawer, scrim)
  • Esc and the scrim close the drawer, and focus returns to the dock button
  • Follow activity never auto-opens the drawer
  • Before the first fit, panels are width 0 with no flash
  • Topbar grid is 1fr auto 1fr
720bp-md: the sidebar is a left drawer, and one drawer at a time; the panel goes edge to edge; the crumb hides; Needs you shows the count only; Share and theme move into the Account sheet
  • Opening one drawer closes the other
  • The Needs you count has its full accessible name
  • Share and theme can be reached in the Account sheet
  • ≤700 rules have been merged here (Foundations D-NEW: merge 700 into 720). The HelperGroup tone dot replaces the chip
  • Touch targets are 44px on a coarse pointer
400bp-xxs: gutters drop to --sp-3, the user bubble is 88% wide, the pill shows a dot and a short label, menus go full width minus 16px, and the composer folds agent, model and approval into "Message settings" (D-NEW-02)
  • Tables and code blocks scroll inside their wrapper, and the page does not scroll sideways
  • Request actions are stacked (≤520)
  • Bottom bar shows icons only (≤520)
  • Popovers fit on screen and are not clipped by the viewport edge
390, keyboard openvisualViewport height under 75% of innerHeight: the bottom bar hides, and the docked request goes compact when it needs more than 45% of the space above the keyboard and composer
  • The textarea caret stays visible while typing 10 lines
  • A request that arrives while typing does not take focus, and its buttons stay above the keyboard
  • The mention and slash menus open upward within the visible viewport
  • Closing the keyboard restores the bottom bar within one frame after the visualViewport resize
  • iOS Safari and Android Chrome both pass
  • At each width, zoom to 200% and check that text reflows. At 320 CSS px wide (400% zoom on 1280) there is no loss of content or function (WCAG 1.4.10).
  • Text spacing override (line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing .12em, word spacing .16em) clips no label (WCAG 1.4.12).
  • Rotating a phone or tablet keeps the open drawer, focus and draft.

3. Build plan by phase

Phases follow convo-v3-plan.html and the build order board. Each component's phase tag is in its own block. Where the board and a block disagree, the block's tag is used here and the clash is listed in the Conflict check (C-10, C-11). Components that are still blocked on backend work ship as disabled controls or stay hidden, then light up without a redesign. Panel and Data components are listed by section until their ids exist.

BE-01 (credentials on fetch and EventSource, CORS for the exact origin) is "now". It is not a phase item. It blocks production auth on its own and must land before any P1 PR merges to a shared environment.

P0: True to the contract

deriveP0 styles/v2/tokens.css, base.css · lib/* contract fixes · no backend

Tokens, the stylesheet pipeline and the contract fixes that make today's UI match the data. P0 needs no backend work, so it can start today.

Scope

  • Tokens: Theme mechanism, Semantic colors, Helper tones, Type presets, Spacing, Layout constants, Radii, Shadows, Z-index, Motion tokens, Animation inventory, Icon
  • Pipeline and a11y base: Stylesheet pipeline (steps for P0), Focus styles, Contrast
  • Contract fixes from the build order board (each is the P0 slice of a P1 block):
    • Remove invented fields: PendingRequest data, Entry union
    • Approval mode and Esc copy: ApprovalModePicker, ToolApprovalCard (D-06)
    • Requests rendered from options[]: ToolApprovalCard, QuestionCard
    • Failure card by reason: TurnFailureCard, ErrorRef
    • Sandboxed visualization: VisualizationCard

Dependencies

None. BE-01 runs in parallel.

Suggested PRs

  1. tokens.css: every new token (spacing, z, motion, --ink-3, --accent-fg, --on-accent) and the dark block parity unit test.
  2. Focus ring, .sr-only, the skip link and the reduced-motion block in base.css.
  3. Contrast swaps: filled buttons to --accent-fg, and small text to --ink-2.
  4. Contract fixes for requests (invented fields out, options[] in, audit label punctuation).
  5. TurnFailureCard by reason, and ErrorRef.
  6. Sandboxed visualization frame, with tokens passed in (Foundations D-NEW: pass tokens into visualization frame).

Exit criteria

  • No literal color left in styles/v2 outside tokens.css (grep check in CI).
  • The parity test passes for the two dark blocks.
  • Every pair in the contrast table meets its rule in both themes.
  • No component reads a field that is missing from shared/contracts.ts.
  • Reduced motion sets every --dur-* to 0s.

P2: Multi-agent clarity and trust

deriveP2 agents sheet, tools shelf, viewer, share, partial answers, cost

Shows who is doing what, why and what it cost.

Scope

  • Agent tints, Share, Partial answer, BatchBar and BatchReviewSheet, Read-only viewer, All agents sheet, Tiled helper view, DelegationSettings, Per-helper cost, McpSettings and tools shelf
  • Edit and delete in AgentDialog and AgentMenu
  • Receipt, privacy and health blocks in Panel

Dependencies

BE-05 (partial answers, retry step), BE-06 (MCP status, sign-in), BE-07 (agent edit and delete), BE-08 (helper cost, exact tree), BE-09 (viewer), BE-10 (delegation per session), BE-19 (Share), BE-20 (privacy findings), BE-21 (rate-limit reset), BE-NEW: roster facts, BE-NEW-S1 (provider re-auth).

Suggested PRs

  1. Read-only viewer bar and "Waiting on owner" (BE-09).
  2. Share popover (BE-19). Until then the button is removed, not left as a no-op.
  3. All agents sheet, then edit and delete (BE-07, roster facts).
  4. McpSettings scope tabs and badges (data today), then LED and sign-in (BE-06).
  5. Partial answer and retry step (BE-05).
  6. Per-helper cost and delegation label (BE-08, BE-10).

Exit criteria

  • A non-owner can open a shared chat and can't send, answer or stop anything.
  • A failed MCP server shows its state in the shelf and the tray.
  • Editing an agent keeps its handle, and old mentions still resolve.
  • Cost cells show "—" until BE-08 and BE-11 data exists, and never 0.

P3: Safety nets for long sessions

proposalP3 behind a flag (D-03)

Drawn now so the layout leaves room for them. They ship behind a flag after the backend work (D-03).

Scope

  • CitationChip and SourcesList, FileCard and canvas link, TurnOutline, ThreadSearch, ConnectedTools and Capabilities (dev mode, D-04)
  • Checkpoint restore action in AnswerActions; thinking duration in ThinkingBlock
  • Side canvas in Panel

Dependencies

BE-11 (cost in currency, thinking duration), BE-12 (checkpoints and restore), BE-13 (citations), BE-14 (versioned files). BE-16 content search for ThreadSearch across unloaded turns.

Suggested PRs

  1. Feature flag plumbing (autopilot=true style, per D-03).
  2. TurnOutline and ThreadSearch (client only on loaded turns).
  3. Citations (BE-13).
  4. Checkpoints and restore (BE-12), tested on real file changes before the flag is removed.
  5. Side canvas (BE-14).

Exit criteria

  • With the flag off, no P3 element renders and no P3 request is made.
  • Restore has been tested on real file changes in both a success and a conflict case.
  • Mod+F behavior is settled per conflict C-01.

CSS consolidation track

This track runs alongside P0 to P2. Each step is one PR with a light and dark check. The order comes from the build order board and Stylesheet pipeline.

  1. Port sheets to styles/v2/sheet.css.
  2. Port request cards to request.css.
  3. Port visualizations and documents to content.css.
  4. Port the slash menu, select and error card to feedback.css and base.css.
  5. Delete the duplicate classes that v2 now neutralizes (.composer, .menu, .request-card and others), and .visually-hidden. This happens only after the last port.
  6. Drop Tailwind and shadcn after replacing Preflight with a short reset (Foundations D-NEW: Tailwind).
  7. Move the 11 legacy files from lucide-react (stroke 2) to the v2 Icon (stroke 1.75).
  8. Merge the ≤700 queries into ≤720 as each surface ports.

6. Conflict check

These clashes come from scanning the decisions, shortcuts and phase tags across the finished parts. Each row gives a recommended resolution. The owning part applies the change in its next revision. Until then, this table decides.

#ClashWhereRecommendation
C-01D-NEW-S11 binds Mod+F to in-thread search with focus in the stream or the composer. Browser find already owns Mod+F. The Shell rule says mod combos fire while typing (skipFields false), so Mod+F would take over browser find from the textarea too.ThreadSearch, KeymapAdopt D-NEW-SH-02. Mod+F opens ThreadSearch only when the P3 flag is on and focus is inside the message list. It never fires from the textarea or any other field, so register it with skipFields: true as an exception to the mod-key rule. A second Mod+F while search is open is not prevented, so browser find still works. It also appears in the shortcut sheet under "Conversation". Before virtualization this is safe. Once the list is windowed (D-NEW-SH-03), browser find misses unrendered turns, so ThreadSearch becomes the main path. Recheck the binding at that point.
C-02Stream shows 20 lines for a collapsed code block. D-08 sets a 30-line threshold.CodeBlockThese are consistent and are two separate values. A block with more than 30 lines collapses (CODE_COLLAPSE_LINES = 30, D-08). A collapsed block shows its first 20 lines (D-NEW-S4). A 31-line block shows 20 lines plus "Show 11 more lines". No block ever hides fewer than 11 lines, which is why the gap is kept. Add CODE_PREVIEW_LINES = 20 next to the threshold, so neither value is a literal.
C-03D-NEW-S8 changes the work-group summary from the wireframe's "Read 3 docs" to "called {n} tools".WorkGroupKeep the generic copy for P1. The data carries no tool category, and a verb map keyed by tool name breaks for MCP tools with custom names. Follow-up: ask the backend for a category on tool items (read, search, write, run, other) as part of BE-04, then switch to verbs with "called {n} tools" as the fallback. Flag the change to design so the high-fidelity pass (D-01) uses the generic copy.
C-04D-NEW-S9 keeps follow-ups sending. The wireframe note says they fill the composer.Follow-ups, SuggestedQuestionsKeep sending, as today, which also matches askSuggestion in Composer. While a turn runs, a follow-up click queues (D-05), and never steers. Add a secondary path to edit a follow-up before sending: Alt+click or the row's "Edit first" menu item fills the composer. Update the wireframe note.
C-05g then n and ? are defined in Shell (D-NEW-7) and in Requests. Both say "outside fields, 1000ms", so they agree. Risk: ? on some layouts needs Shift, and g collides with screen-reader browse-mode quick keys (NVDA, JAWS use g for graphics).Keymap, NeedsYouTrayKeep one definition, in the Shell keymap, and have Requests link to it. Match ? on event.key === "?", not on key code. In screen-reader browse mode the reader takes the keys first, which is expected. Keep Shift+Tab to the dock and the Needs you button as the paths that don't depend on the shortcut. Add a Settings toggle to turn single-key shortcuts off (WCAG 2.1.4).
C-06mod+Enter is defined three times: Steer or send in the composer (CP-10), send an edit in message edit mode (Stream), and send Revise in the plan card (Requests).Steer, UserActions, PlanApprovalCardNo real clash, because each one is scoped to the focused textarea. Rule: mod+Enter means "submit this field". It is handled by the field's own onKeyDown and never by useHotkeys, and it calls stopPropagation. List all three in the shortcut sheet under their context. Edit mode must not steer: sending an edit while running queues the edit, per BE-03 rules.
C-07Some parts add their own polite regions: palette count, thread search count, mention count (CP-07), the pre.ag-live helper live tail, and the .nad-stage note.Palette, ThreadSearch, MentionMenu, AgentsPanel, AgentDialogKeep the counts local to their open widget, since they only speak while it has focus. Remove aria-live from pre.ag-live. It streams helper output, which breaks the rule that streaming text is never read aloud. The transcript tab uses aria-busy like the main list instead. The .nad-stage note may stay polite, because it changes once per save.
C-08Decision ids clash. Shell uses D-NEW-1..7 and Composer uses D-NEW-01..12, so "D-NEW-7" and "D-NEW-07" name different things. Foundations and Requests use names instead of numbers.All partsUse prefixed ids in the register (SH-, CP-, S, AG-, SH-0x for this part). Each part should rename its ids to the prefixed form on its next edit. Until then, cross-part links cite the part name with the id.
C-09The waiting announcement is "Needs your approval" on the States board and "Waiting on you" in Shell.TopbarUse "Waiting on you". It covers questions and plans. The specific request text ("Permission needed: {title}.") carries the approval detail.
C-10The build order board puts "Failure card by reason" and "Sandboxed visualization" in P0. The blocks tag them P1.TurnFailureCard, VisualizationCardDo both. The contract slice (reason mapping, sandbox attributes) ships in P0 with no new UI. The v3 visual design ships in P1. The P0 scope lists them this way.
C-11The board puts "Goal strip, long-chat nav" in P1 and "Batch review, tiled helpers" in P3. The blocks tag TurnOutline and ThreadSearch P3, and BatchReviewSheet and tiled helpers P2.TurnOutline, ThreadSearch, BatchBar, Tiled helpersFollow the blocks. Long-chat nav in P1 is JumpToLatest and Older work groups. The outline and search need virtualization first (D-NEW-SH-03). Batch and tiles are client-only, so they can ship in P2. Update the board.
C-12Chip labels hide at ≤1100 viewport (Foundations bp-xl) and at ≤520 composer width (CP-02).Breakpoints, Action barUse one rule: measure the composer width with a ResizeObserver. Labels hide below 560px of composer width, which covers the 1100 case with both side columns open. The fold into "Message settings" happens below 400px of composer width. Drop the viewport rule from bp-xl.
C-13The States board says "mod+J jumps to" a new request. The Shell keymap binds mod+J to New chat.Keymap, States boardKeep mod+J as New chat (exists). The key path to a request is g n, or Shift+Tab from the composer. Fix the board note.
C-14Esc order is written three ways: Composer's keyboard table, Stream ("search before any other Esc"), and Requests (D-06, stopPropagation). The panel-close step and the stop-turn step both sit at the bottom of Composer's list.Send and Stop, ThreadSearch, Requests timingUse the single Esc stack (D-NEW-SH-01). Closing the side panel counts as a popover or drawer layer, so it comes before stopping the turn. Stop runs only when focus is in the composer and no layer is open.
C-15D-NEW-AG-07 ignores a scrim click while the dialog is dirty, but Esc still closes it and discards the changes.AgentDialogKeep it. Esc is an explicit key, not a stray click. Show "Discard changes?" with "Discard" and "Keep editing" only if the draft is over 200 characters. Otherwise Esc closes at once.

7. QA acceptance checklist

Run this for every phase exit, on Chrome, Safari and Firefox (latest), iOS Safari and Android Chrome.

  • Both themes: every surface in light, dark, and system with a live OS switch. No literal colors, and sandboxed visuals re-render on a theme change.
  • All widths: every row of the QA matrix passes, with no horizontal page scroll at 400 and 390.
  • Keyboard only: with no pointer, a user can send, queue, steer, stop, answer each request kind, open and close every popover, sheet and drawer, use the tray, create an agent, attach a file, and open every folded block. Focus is visible at every step and never lands on body.
  • Focus return: each row of the focus table returns focus to the listed target.
  • Esc: each step of the Esc stack runs alone, and one Esc never does two things.
  • Screen reader passes: VoiceOver with Safari (macOS and iOS), NVDA with Firefox or Chrome, TalkBack with Chrome. Landmarks are listed as in §1. A full turn gives "Working" then "Done", with no streamed text read aloud. A docked request is announced once. Every icon button has its name.
  • Reduced motion: every row of the reduced motion table holds, and busy states are still visible without animation.
  • Slow network (Chrome "Slow 3G") and reconnect: drop the connection during a stream. The pill says "Reconnecting", request controls disable with the reconnect copy, and the stream resyncs with no duplicate messages. The draft and the queue survive.
  • Read-only viewer (BE-09): the composer is replaced by the viewer bar, requests show "Waiting on owner", and no send, answer, stop, edit or delete control can be reached by mouse or keyboard.
  • Long chats: a 200-turn chat with code, tools and helpers opens within the budget in §9. Scrolling holds 60fps on the reference machine. JumpToLatest, the outline (P3) and search find turns outside the rendered window.
  • Streaming, no layout jump: while tokens arrive, the content above the stream does not move (CLS 0 for content above the viewport bottom). Auto-follow keeps the bottom pinned only when the user was at the bottom. The work group fold after 600ms does not move the user's reading position. Code blocks reserve their collapsed height as soon as the fence opens.
  • Zoom 200% and 400% reflow, and text spacing override, pass (see §2).
  • Touch: every target meets 44px on a coarse pointer, and hover-only actions are always visible on the last turn.
  • Contrast: the pairs in §1 contrast are spot-checked with a color picker in both themes, and in forced colors mode.
  • Axe or Lighthouse accessibility scan has no critical or serious issues. This is a floor, not a pass (see the note at the top).

8. Definition of done for each component

A component block is done when every item holds. Reviewers tick this list in the PR description.

  • Matches its block: anatomy, sizes, tokens, states, copy and data interface. Any change goes back into the spec in the same PR.
  • Uses tokens only. No literal color, spacing, z-index or duration in its CSS.
  • Every state in its States table can be reached in Storybook or a test fixture, in light and dark.
  • Every acceptance item in its block is an automated test (unit, component or Playwright), or is marked "manual" with a reason.
  • Keyboard and a11y subsection implemented: roles, names, focus return and key paths. Icon-only buttons pass the label lint rule.
  • Announcements go through announce() only, and use the exact strings in §1.
  • Reduced motion and forced colors checked.
  • Works at 400px and inside the ≤900 drawer, where it can appear there.
  • Backend-blocked parts show their fallback state and are behind a capability check, not a commented-out block.
  • Proposal values cite their D-id in code comments, so the value can be found when the decision changes.
  • No new legacy class names (pipeline rule), and no Tailwind classes.
  • Render cost stays within the performance budget for stream components.

9. Performance budgets

proposal D-NEW-SH-04. None of these numbers are measured yet. The reference machine is a mid-range 2022 laptop with 4x CPU throttle in Chrome DevTools for the "low end" column.

MetricDefinitionBudgetLow end
Time to first token displayFirst token event received to its glyphs painted≤ 50ms≤ 100ms
Send to WorkingSend pressed to the pill and placeholder showing the starting state≤ 100ms (no network wait)≤ 150ms
Stream render costMain-thread time per token batch. Batch tokens per animation frame, and never re-render per token≤ 4ms per frame at 60fps≤ 8ms
Markdown reparseOnly the last open block is re-parsed on each batch; closed blocks are memoized≤ 2ms per batch for a 4,000-word answer≤ 5ms
Syntax highlightshiki runs on a closed fence only, off the main thread or in idle time; plain text while open≤ 16ms per block, grammar lazy-loaded≤ 40ms
Open a chatRoute change to the last turn painted≤ 400ms for 50 turns, ≤ 800ms for 200 turns≤ 1.2s for 200 turns
Input latencyKeypress in the composer to paint, during a stream≤ 50ms (INP)≤ 100ms
Layout shiftCLS during a full turn, for content above the viewport bottom00
JS added by v3Initial route bundle, gzip, excluding lazy grammars and P3≤ 60 KB

When to virtualize the list

D-NEW-SH-03. Proposed rule: render every turn up to 150 turns, or 3,000 DOM nodes in the list, whichever comes first. Above that, switch to a windowed list that keeps the latest 40 turns and the viewport's neighbours (2 screens above and below) mounted. The rest become measured placeholders, with heights cached by turn id.

  • The streaming turn, any turn with a docked request anchor, and any turn holding focus are always mounted.
  • Heights come from a ResizeObserver per mounted turn. Unknown heights use a per-kind estimate and are corrected without moving the reading position (scroll anchoring).
  • Screen readers: a turn that is not mounted can't be read in browse mode. Keep the turn article headings in a hidden outline list, so a user can jump to a turn by heading. ThreadSearch (P3) and BE-16 content search cover find.
  • Browser find misses unmounted turns. This is why C-01 is rechecked when virtualization lands.
  • Before that point, the older work group collapse (sm-older) is the first way to cut DOM size.
